cards.en: If he meant talaq, it is one final talaq, unless he meant three. If he meant zihar (likening his wife to his mother, taught in the next part), it is zihar. If he meant making her forbidden, or meant nothing, it is an oath that makes him a mu'li.

cards.ask: He said "You are haram to me". What is it, by what he meant?
cards.source: وإن قال: أردت الطلاق فهي تطليقة بائنة إلا أن ينوي الثلاث وإن قال: أردت الظهار فهو ظهار وإن قال: أردت التحريم أو لم أرد به شيئا فهو يمين يصير بها موليا
cards.why: Talaq gives one final talaq, zihar is zihar, and forbidding or nothing is an oath of ila'.

cards.ask: Harun tells his wife "You are haram to me" and says he meant nothing by it. Then he keeps away from her for four months. What happens?
options: She is separated by one final talaq, as in any ila'
source: أو لم أرد به شيئا فهو يمين يصير بها موليا
وإن لم يقربها حتى مضت أربعة أشهر بانت منه بتطليقة
cards.why: Meaning nothing makes it an ila' oath, so four months away separates her by one talaq.

lessons.title: Khul': a wife freeing herself for payment

cards.title: What khul' is
cards.ar: وخافا أن لا يقيما حدود الله فلا بأس أن تفتدي نفسها منه بمال يخلعها به
cards.en: Khul': if husband and wife are at odds and fear they will not keep within the limits Allah has set, there is no harm in the wife freeing herself from him with money in return for which he releases her.

cards.title: What it does
cards.ar: وقع بالخلع تطليقة بائنة ولزمها المال
cards.en: Khul' counts as one final (ba'in) talaq, and she must pay the money agreed.

cards.title: Whose fault
cards.ar: وإن كان النشوز من قبله كره له أن يأخذ منها عوضا وإن كان النشوز من قبلها كره له
cards.en: Nushuz is a spouse turning against the other and treating them badly. If the nushuz is from the husband's side, it is disliked for him to take any payment from her. If it is from her side, it is disliked for him to take more than he gave her (her mahr). If he does take more, it is still valid in court.

cards.ask: The trouble came from Fatin's side. For a khul' she pays her husband 2,000 dirhams, though his mahr to her was 1,000. Is it valid?
options: Valid in court, but it is disliked for him to take more than he gave
Invalid: he must give back the extra
Perfectly fine, with no dislike at all
cards.source: أكثر مما أعطاها فإن فعل ذلك جاز في القضاء
cards.why: Taking more than he gave is disliked, but if he does, it is valid in court.

cards.ask: The trouble came from the husband's side, and his wife asks for a khul'. What does the book say about him taking payment?
options: It is disliked for him to take anything
He may take up to the mahr
He must take double the mahr
cards.source: وإن كان النشوز من قبله كره له أن يأخذ منها عوضا
cards.why: When the fault is his, it is disliked for him to take any payment from her.

cards.title: A talaq for money
cards.ar: وإن طلقها على مال فقبلت وقع الطلاق ولزمها المال وكان الطلاق بائنا
cards.en: If he divorces her in return for money and she accepts, the talaq happens, she owes the money, and the talaq is final.

cards.title: When the payment is not valid
cards.ar: وإذا بطل العوض في الخلع مثل أن تخالع المرأة المسلمة على خمر أو خنزير فلا شيء للزوج والفرقة بائنة وإن بطل العوض في الطلاق كان رجعيا
cards.en: If the payment ('iwad) in a khul' is not valid, like a Muslim woman offering wine or pork, the husband gets nothing and the separation is final. If the payment fails in a talaq for money, the talaq is revocable.

cards.title: What can be paid
cards.ar: وما جاز أن يكون مهرا جاز أن يكون بدلا في الخلع
cards.en: Anything that may be given as a mahr may be given as the payment in a khul'.

cards.ask: Is the separation final or revocable?
items: A talaq for 500 dirhams, which she accepts
A Muslim woman's khul' for wine
source: وقع بالخلع تطليقة بائنة
وكان الطلاق بائنا
فلا شيء للزوج والفرقة بائنة وإن بطل العوض في الطلاق كان رجعيا
cards.why: Khul' is always final, and so is a talaq for valid money. Only a talaq whose payment fails is revocable.

cards.ask: Rania, a Muslim, makes a khul' with her husband for a payment of wine. What does her husband get?
options: Nothing, and the separation is final
cards.source: مثل أن تخالع المرأة المسلمة على خمر أو خنزير فلا شيء للزوج والفرقة بائنة
cards.why: Wine cannot be a payment for a Muslim, so he gets nothing, and the separation is still final.

cards.title: "For what is in my hand"
cards.ar: فإن قالت له: خالعني على ما في يدي فخالعها ولم يكن في يدها شيء فلا شيء له عليها وإن قالت: خالعني على ما في يدي من مال ولم يكن في يدها شيء ردت عليه مهرها
cards.en: If she says "Make khul' with me for what is in my hand" and her hand is empty, she owes him nothing. If she says "for the money in my hand" and it is empty, she gives him back her mahr.

cards.title: "For the dirhams in my hand"
cards.ar: وإن قالت: خالعني على ما في يدي من دراهم
cards.en: If she says "for the dirhams in my hand" and her hand is empty, she owes three dirhams: "dirhams" means at least three.

cards.ask: He agrees to the khul', and her hand turns out to be empty. What does she owe?
source: فلا شيء له عليها
ردت عليه مهرها
ولم يكن في يدها شيء فعليها ثلاثة دراهم
cards.why: An empty "what" is nothing; "money" means her mahr is returned; "dirhams" means three dirhams.

cards.title: Asking for three, getting one
cards.ar: وإن قالت: طلقني ثلاثا بألف فطلقها واحدة فعليها ثلث الألف وإن قالت: طلقني ثلاثا على ألف فطلقها واحدة فلا شيء عليها عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: If she says "Divorce me three times for (bi) a thousand" and he divorces her once, she owes a third of the thousand. If she says "on condition of ('ala) a thousand" and he divorces her once, she owes nothing, according to Abu Hanifa.

cards.ask: Huda says, "Divorce me three times for 900 dirhams." He divorces her once. What does she owe?
cards.source: طلقني ثلاثا بألف فطلقها واحدة فعليها ثلث الألف
cards.why: With "for", each talaq takes its share: one of three is a third, 300 of 900.

cards.ask: This time Huda says, "Divorce me three times on condition of 900 dirhams." He divorces her once. For Abu Hanifa, what does she owe?
cards.source: طلقني ثلاثا على ألف فطلقها واحدة فلا شيء عليها عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: With "on condition of", the money is for all three together, so one talaq costs her nothing.

cards.title: When he offers it
cards.ar: ولو قال الزوج: طلقي نفسك ثلاثا بألف أو على ألف فطلقت نفسها واحدة لم يقع عليها شيء
cards.en: If the husband says "Divorce yourself three times for (or on condition of) a thousand" and she divorces herself only once, nothing happens at all.

cards.title: Mutual release (mubara'a)
cards.ar: والمبارأة كالخلع والخلع كالمبارأة يسقطان كل حق لكل واحد من الزوجين على الآخر مما يتعلق بالنكاح عند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله إلا نفقة العدة
cards.en: Mubara'a is when husband and wife release each other. For Abu Hanifa, mubara'a and khul' are alike: both drop every claim each spouse has on the other from the marriage, except the nafaqa (living costs) of her 'idda. Note: Abu Yusuf says mubara'a drops them but khul' does not; Muhammad says neither drops anything except what they named.

cards.ask: After a khul', for Abu Hanifa, which claims are dropped?

options.text: Mahr she was still owed
Other claims either spouse has from the marriage
The same claims, after a mubara'a instead
Her nafaqa (living costs) during the 'idda

cards.source: يسقطان كل حق لكل واحد من الزوجين على الآخر مما يتعلق بالنكاح عند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله إلا نفقة العدة
cards.why: Khul' and mubara'a drop every marriage claim on both sides, except her nafaqa for the 'idda.

cards.ask: A husband says, "Divorce yourself three times for 1,000 dirhams." She divorces herself once. What happens?
options: One talaq, and she owes about 333 dirhams
One talaq, and she owes nothing
cards.source: ولو قال الزوج: طلقي نفسك ثلاثا بألف أو على ألف فطلقت نفسها واحدة لم يقع عليها شيء
cards.why: When he offers three for money and she takes only one, nothing happens at all.

cards.title: Like my mother's back
cards.ar: إذا قال الزوج لامرأته: أنت علي كظهر أمي فقد حرمت عليه ولا يحل له وطؤها ولا لمسها ولا تقبيلها حتى يكفر عن ظهاره
cards.en: Zihar is when a husband tells his wife "You are to me like my mother's back": an old Arab saying that meant she was as forbidden to him as his mother. When he says it, she becomes forbidden to him. He may not be intimate with her, touch her or kiss her until he pays the kaffara (a set act of expiation that wipes out the wrong).

cards.ask: After zihar, when is the wife allowed to him again? Complete it.
cards.ar: ولا يحل له وطؤها ولا لمسها ولا تقبيلها حتى ____ عن ظهاره
cards.source: ولا يحل له وطؤها ولا لمسها ولا تقبيلها حتى يكفر عن ظهاره
cards.why: يكفر: she is forbidden to him until he pays the kaffara for his zihar.

cards.title: If he is intimate before paying
cards.ar: فإن وطئها قبل أن يكفر استغفر الله تعالى ولا شيء عليه غير الكفارة الأولى ولا يعاودها حتى يكفر
cards.en: If he is intimate with her before paying the kaffara, he asks Allah's forgiveness. He owes nothing more than the first kaffara, but he must not go back to her again until he pays it.

cards.title: The 'returning'
cards.ar: والعود الذي تجب به الكفارة أن يعزم على وطئها
cards.en: The Qur'an speaks of men who say zihar and then "return". The returning ('awd) that makes the kaffara due is that he makes up his mind to live with her as husband and wife again.

cards.ask: Hamid said zihar to his wife, then was intimate with her before paying any kaffara. What does he owe now?
options: He asks Allah's forgiveness and still owes just the one kaffara
cards.source: فإن وطئها قبل أن يكفر استغفر الله تعالى ولا شيء عليه غير الكفارة الأولى
cards.why: He asks forgiveness and owes nothing beyond the first kaffara, which he must still pay before going back to her.

cards.title: Other words that are zihar
cards.ar: فهو مظاهر وكذلك إن شبهها بمن لا يحل له النظر على التأييد من محارمه مثل أخته أو عمته أو أمه من الرضاعة
cards.en: Comparing her to his mother's stomach or thigh is also zihar, and so is comparing her to any close relative he may never marry, such as his sister, his aunt or his milk-mother. The same goes if he compares a part of her (her head, face, neck, half or a third of her) to his mother's back.

cards.ask: Which of these sayings, from a husband to his wife, are zihar?

options.text: "You are to me like my mother's back"
"You are to me like my sister's back"
"Your head is to me like my mother's back"
"You are to me like my mother's stomach"
"You are to me like my mother", meaning only respect

source: وإذا قال: أنت علي كبطن أمي أو كفخذها
مثل أخته أو عمته أو أمه من الرضاعة
وكذلك إن قال: رأسك علي كظهر أمي
أو وجهك أو رقبتك أو نصفك أو ثلثك
cards.why: His mother's back or stomach, a forbidden relative like a sister, and a part of her like the head are all zihar. "Like my mother" meant as respect is only what he meant.

cards.title: "Like my mother" depends on what he meant
cards.ar: وإن قال: أنت علي مثل أمي رجع إلى نيته فإن قال أردت الكرامة فهو كما قال وإن قال: أردت الظهار فهو ظهار وإن قال: أردت الطلاق فهو طلاق بائن وإن لم يكن له نية فليس شيء
cards.en: If he says "You are to me like my mother", it depends on his intention (niyya). If he meant respect, it is as he says. If he meant zihar, it is zihar. If he meant divorce, it is a ba'in divorce (one that ends the marriage at once). If he meant nothing, it is nothing.

cards.ask: Umar says to his wife "You are to me like my mother". What is it, if he meant...
cards.source: رجع إلى نيته فإن قال أردت الكرامة فهو كما قال وإن قال: أردت الظهار فهو ظهار وإن قال: أردت الطلاق فهو طلاق بائن وإن لم يكن له نية فليس شيء
cards.why: It follows his intention: respect or no intention is nothing, zihar is zihar, and divorce is a ba'in divorce.

cards.title: Only from a wife
cards.ar: ولا يكون الظهار إلا من زوجته فإن ظاهر من أمته لم يكن مظاهرا ومن قال لنسائه: أنتن علي كظهر أمي كان مظاهرا من جماعتهن وعليه لكل واحدة منهن كفارة
cards.en: Zihar is only from a wife. In al-Quduri's time a man could own a slave woman; saying it to her was not zihar. If he says it to all his wives together, it is zihar from every one of them, and he owes a separate kaffara for each.

cards.ask: Sa'id has two wives. He says to them both, "You are to me like my mother's back." How many kaffaras does he owe?
cards.source: كان مظاهرا من جماعتهن وعليه لكل واحدة منهن كفارة
cards.why: He has made zihar from each wife, so he owes one kaffara for each of them: two.

cards.ask: Tariq tells his wife "You are to me like my mother" and says he meant nothing by it. What follows?
options: Nothing: without an intention it is nothing
It is zihar and he owes a kaffara
cards.source: وإن لم يكن له نية فليس شيء
cards.why: "Like my mother" goes back to his intention, and with no intention it is nothing. Only "like my mother's back" is zihar on its own.

cards.title: Three steps of the kaffara
cards.ar: وكفارة الظهار: عتق رقبة فإن لم يجد فصيام شهرين متتابعين فإن لم يستطع
cards.en: The kaffara of zihar is to free a slave (raqaba). In al-Quduri's time slavery existed, and freeing a slave was a great act of worship. If he cannot find one, he fasts two months in a row. If he cannot do that, he feeds sixty poor people. All of this must be done before he touches his wife.

cards.ask: Put the kaffara of zihar in order: what he tries first, then next, then last.
steps: Fast two months in a row
source: عتق رقبة فإن لم يجد فصيام شهرين متتابعين فإن لم يستطع
أطعم ستين مسكينا
كل ذلك قبل المسيس
cards.why: Freeing comes first; if he cannot find a slave he fasts two months in a row; if he cannot fast he feeds sixty poor people, all before touching his wife.

cards.title: Which slave counts
cards.ar: ويجزئ في ذلك عتق الرقبة الكافرة والمسلمة والذكر والأنثى والصغير والكبير ولا تجزئ العمياء ولا المقطوعة اليدين أو الرجلين
cards.en: Freeing a non-Muslim or a Muslim, a male or a female, a child or an adult all count. Freeing someone who is blind, or who has lost both hands or both feet, does not count.

cards.title: Some lost limbs count, others do not
cards.ar: ويجوز الأصم والمقطوع إحدى اليدين وإحدى الرجلين من خلاف ولا يجوز مقطوع إبهامي اليدين ولا المجنون الذي لا يعقل
cards.en: A deaf person counts. So does one who has lost one hand and one foot on opposite sides. One who has lost both thumbs does not count, nor an insane person who cannot understand.

cards.ask: Does freeing this person count for the kaffara?
items: A man missing one hand and the foot on the other side
An insane man who cannot understand
source: ويجزئ في ذلك عتق الرقبة الكافرة والمسلمة والذكر والأنثى والصغير والكبير ولا تجزئ العمياء
ويجوز الأصم والمقطوع إحدى اليدين وإحدى الرجلين من خلاف ولا يجوز مقطوع إبهامي اليدين ولا المجنون الذي لا يعقل
cards.why: Deaf, young, non-Muslim, and one hand and one foot on opposite sides all count. Blind, both thumbs lost, or insane do not.

cards.title: Those already on the way to freedom
cards.ar: ولا يجوز عتق المدبر وأم الولد والمكاتب الذي أدى بعض المال فإن أعتق مكاتبا لم يود شيئا جاز فإن اشترى أباه أو ابنه ينوي بالشراء الكفارة جاز عنها
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time some slaves were already partly on the way to freedom: a mudabbar (promised freedom when the owner dies), an umm walad (a slave woman who bore her owner a child) and a mukatab (buying his freedom by instalments). Freeing a mudabbar, an umm walad, or a mukatab who has paid some of his price does not count. A mukatab who has paid nothing counts. If he buys his own father or son (who become free on purchase) intending the kaffara, it counts.

cards.ask: Nabil owes a zihar kaffara. He buys his own father, who is enslaved, intending the purchase as his kaffara. Does it count?
options: Yes: buying his father with the intention of the kaffara counts
No: his father would become free anyway
cards.source: فإن اشترى أباه أو ابنه ينوي بالشراء الكفارة جاز عنها
cards.why: Buying his father or son while intending the kaffara counts for it.

cards.title: Freeing half at a time
cards.ar: وإن أعتق نصف عبد مشترك عن الكفارة وضمن قيمة باقية فأعتقه لم يجز عند أبي حنيفة وإن أعتق نصف عبده عن كفارته ثم أعتق باقية عنها جاز
cards.en: If he frees his half of a slave he shares with someone, pays for the rest and frees it, it does not count, according to Abu Hanifa. But if he frees half of his own slave for the kaffara and then the other half too, it counts.

cards.title: If he touches his wife in between
cards.ar: وإن أعتق نصف عبده عن كفارته ثم جامع التي ظاهر منها ثم أعتق باقية لم يجز عند أب حنيفة
cards.en: If he frees half of his slave for the kaffara, is then intimate with the wife he made zihar from, and only then frees the other half, it does not count, according to Abu Hanifa: the kaffara must be complete before he touches her.

cards.ask: Hassan owns a slave alone. He frees half of him for his zihar kaffara, and a week later frees the other half for it, without touching his wife in between. Does it count?
options: Yes: half and then the rest, both for the kaffara, counts
No: a slave must be freed all at once
cards.source: وإن أعتق نصف عبده عن كفارته ثم أعتق باقية عنها جاز
cards.why: Freeing half of his own slave and then the rest, both for the kaffara, counts.

cards.ask: Which of these count as the 'freeing' of a zihar kaffara?

options.text: Freeing a young child
Freeing a mukatab who has paid nothing yet
Buying his son with the intention of the kaffara
Freeing an umm walad
Freeing a mudabbar
Freeing a blind man

source: والصغير والكبير
فإن أعتق مكاتبا لم يود شيئا جاز
ولا يجوز عتق المدبر وأم الولد
ولا تجزئ العمياء
cards.why: A child, a mukatab who has paid nothing, and his own son bought for the kaffara count. An umm walad, a mudabbar and a blind man do not.

cards.title: Two months in a row
cards.ar: وإذا لم يجد المظاهر ما يعتق فكفارته صوم شهرين متتابعين ليس فيهما شهر رمضان ولا يوم الفطر ولا يوم النحر ولا أيام التشريق
cards.en: If the man who made zihar cannot find a slave to free, he fasts two months in a row. They must not include the month of Ramadan, the day of Eid al-Fitr, the Day of Sacrifice (Eid al-Adha), or the days of tashriq (the three days after it).

cards.ask: Ibrahim must fast for his zihar. He starts on the first day of Sha'ban, so his two months would be Sha'ban and Ramadan. Does this work?
options: No: the two months must not include Ramadan
Yes: any two months in a row will do
Yes, if he fasts an extra day
cards.source: صوم شهرين متتابعين ليس فيهما شهر رمضان
cards.why: The two months of the kaffara must not include Ramadan, so he must choose two other months in a row.

cards.title: When he must start again
cards.ar: فإن جامع التي ظاهر منها في خلال الشهرين ليلا عامدا أو نهارا ناسيا استأنف الصوم عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد وإن أفطر يوما بعذر أو بغير عذر استأنف
cards.en: If during the two months he is intimate with the wife he made zihar from, at night on purpose or by day forgetting, he starts the fast again, according to Abu Hanifa and Muhammad. If he misses even one day, with an excuse or without, he starts again.

cards.ask: Musa has fasted 40 days of his two months. He falls ill and misses one day. What must he do?
options: Make up the one day at the end
cards.source: وإن أفطر يوما بعذر أو بغير عذر استأنف
cards.why: Missing a day, with an excuse or without, breaks the run of two months, so he starts again.

cards.title: A slave's zihar
cards.ar: وإن ظاهر العبد لم يجزه في الكفارة إلا الصوم فإن أعتق المولى عنه أو أطعم لم يجزه
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, an enslaved man owned no property of his own. So if he made zihar, only fasting counted for his kaffara. Even if his master freed a slave or fed the poor for him, it did not count.

cards.title: Feeding sixty poor people
cards.ar: وإذا لم يستطع المظاهر الصيام أطعم ستين مسكينا كل مسكين نصف صاع من بر أو صاعا من تمر أو شعير أو قيمة تلك
cards.en: If he cannot fast, he feeds sixty poor people. Each gets half a sa' of wheat, or a whole sa' of dates or barley (a sa' is a measure of volume), or the value of that.

cards.ask: Which food is given as half a sa'? Complete it.
cards.ar: كل مسكين نصف صاع من ____ أو صاعا من تمر أو شعير
cards.source: كل مسكين نصف صاع من بر أو صاعا من تمر أو شعير
cards.why: بر: half a sa' of wheat, but a whole sa' of dates or barley.

cards.title: Meals, one man, and touching during the feeding
cards.ar: فإن غداهم وعشاهم جاز قليلا ما أكلوا أو كثيرا فإن أعطى مسكينا واحدا ستين يوما أجزأه وإن أعطاه في يوم واحد لم يجزه إلا عن يومه وإن قرب التي ظاهر منها في خلال الإطعام لم يستأنف
cards.en: If he gives them lunch and dinner, it counts, whether they eat a little or a lot. Feeding one poor man for sixty days counts. But giving one man everything on a single day counts only for that one day. If he goes near his wife partway through the feeding, he does not start again.

cards.ask: Does this feeding fully count for one zihar kaffara?
items: Lunch and dinner for 60 poor people who eat only a little
Feeding the same poor man every day for 60 days
Giving 60 poor people the value of the food
Giving one poor man all 60 portions on one day
A quarter sa' of wheat each to 60 poor people
source: فإن غداهم وعشاهم جاز قليلا ما أكلوا أو كثيرا فإن أعطى مسكينا واحدا ستين يوما أجزأه وإن أعطاه في يوم واحد لم يجزه إلا عن يومه
نصف صاع من بر
أو قيمة تلك
cards.why: Two meals, one man over sixty days, or the value all count. One man on one day counts only for that day, and each person needs half a sa' of wheat.

cards.title: Two kaffaras at once
cards.ar: ومن وجب عليه كفارتا ظهار فأعتق رقبتين لا ينوي عن إحداهما بعينها جاز عنهما
cards.en: If a man owes two zihar kaffaras and frees two slaves without saying which is for which, both count. It is the same if he fasts four months or feeds 120 poor people. If he does only one kaffara, he may count it for whichever of the two he likes.

cards.ask: Zayd made zihar from both his wives and cannot free a slave or fast. He feeds 120 poor people without saying which wife each meal is for. Does it count?
options: No: he must name each wife
cards.source: أطعم مائة وعشرين مسكينا جاز
cards.why: Feeding 120 poor people covers both kaffaras, even without naming which is for which.

cards.ask: Bakr owes two zihar kaffaras, one for each wife. So far he has fasted two months in a row. What may he do with this fast?
options: Count it for whichever of the two he wishes
Nothing: it counts for neither until he fasts four months
Split it, one month for each
cards.source: وإن أعتق رقبة واحدة أو صام شهرين كان له أن يجعل ذلك عن أيتهما شاء
cards.why: One full kaffara may be counted for whichever of the two he chooses.

lessons.title: Li'an: the oaths of husband and wife

cards.title: When li'an is due
cards.ar: إذا قذف الرجل امرأته بالزنا وهما من أهل الشهادة والمرأة ممن يحد قاذفها أو نفى نسب ولدها وطالبته بموجب القذف فعليه اللعان
cards.en: Qadhf is accusing someone of zina (unlawful relations). Li'an is a set of oaths that husband and wife swear before the judge. It is due when a husband accuses his wife of zina, or denies that her child is his, and she asks the judge to act. Both must be fit to be witnesses, and she must be a woman whose accuser would be punished.

cards.title: If one of them refuses
cards.ar: فإن امتنع منه حبسه الحاكم حتى يلاعن أو يكذب نفسه فيحد وإن لاعن وجب عليها اللعان فإن امتنعت حبسها الحاكم حتى تلاعن أو تصدقه
cards.en: If he refuses li'an, the judge holds him until he swears it, or admits he lied and receives the punishment for qadhf. Once he has sworn, she must swear too. If she refuses, the judge holds her until she swears or agrees that he is right.

cards.ask: Karim accused his wife, and she asked the judge to act. Karim refuses to swear the li'an. What does the judge do?
options: Holds him until he swears or admits he lied
cards.source: فإن امتنع منه حبسه الحاكم حتى يلاعن أو يكذب نفسه فيحد
cards.why: The judge holds him until he swears the li'an, or admits he lied and is punished for qadhf.

cards.title: When there is no li'an
cards.ar: وإذا كان من أهل الشهادة وهي أمة أو كافر أو محدودة في قذف أو كانت ممن لا يحد قاذفها فلا حد عليه في قذفها ولا لعان
cards.en: If he is fit to be a witness but she is a slave woman (in al-Quduri's time), not a Muslim, has once been punished for qadhf herself, or is someone whose accuser is not punished, then there is neither punishment nor li'an for his accusation.

cards.title: The husband's oaths
cards.ar: وصفة اللعان: أن يبتدئ القاضي بالزوج فيشهد أربع مرات يقول في كل مرة: أشهد بالله إني لمن الصادقين فيما رميتها به من الزنا
cards.en: The judge begins with the husband. Four times he says: "I testify by Allah that I am truthful in what I accused her of."

cards.title: The fifth oath, and the wife's oaths
cards.ar: ثم يقول في الخامسة: لعنة الله عليه إن كان من الكاذبين فيما رماها به من الزنا ويشير إليها في جميع ذلك ثم تشهد المرأة أربع مرات
cards.en: The fifth time he says: "The curse of Allah be on him if he is lying." He points to her each time. Then the wife testifies four times that he is lying, and the fifth time she says: "The anger of Allah be on her if he is truthful."

cards.ask: Put the li'an in order.
steps: The husband testifies four times that he is truthful
The husband calls Allah's curse on himself if he is lying
The wife testifies four times that he is lying
The wife calls Allah's anger on herself if he is truthful
source: أن يبتدئ القاضي بالزوج فيشهد أربع مرات
ثم يقول في الخامسة: لعنة الله عليه إن كان من الكاذبين
ثم تشهد المرأة أربع مرات تقول في كل مرة: أشهد بالله إنه لمن الكاذبين
وتقول في الخامسة: إن غضب الله عليها إن كان من الصادقين
فإذا التعنا فرق القاضي بينهما
cards.why: The judge starts with the husband's four oaths and his fifth, then the wife's four and her fifth, and then he separates them.

cards.ask: What does the husband call on himself in his fifth oath? Complete it.
cards.ar: ثم يقول في الخامسة: ____ الله عليه إن كان من الكاذبين
cards.source: ثم يقول في الخامسة: لعنة الله عليه إن كان من الكاذبين
cards.why: لعنة: the husband calls the curse of Allah on himself; the wife's fifth oath is about Allah's anger.

cards.title: The separation
cards.ar: فإذا التعنا فرق القاضي بينهما وكانت الفرقة تطليقه بائنة عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد وقال أبو يوسف: تحريم مؤبد
cards.en: When both have sworn, the judge separates them. For Abu Hanifa and Muhammad the separation is a ba'in divorce (one that ends the marriage at once). Note: Abu Yusuf says it makes her forbidden to him forever.

cards.title: The child, and if he takes it back
cards.ar: وإن كان القذف بولد نفى القاضي نسبه وألحقه بأمه فإن عاد الزوج فأكذب نفسه حده القاضي وحل له أن يتزوجها
cards.en: If the accusation was about a child, the judge cuts the child's nasab (lineage) from the husband and joins it to the mother. If the husband later admits he lied, the judge punishes him for qadhf, and he may marry her again. The same if he is later punished for accusing someone else, or she is punished for zina.

cards.ask: After li'an the judge separated Rami and Layla. A year later Rami admits he lied. What follows?
options: He is punished for qadhf, and he may marry Layla again
He must swear the li'an again
cards.source: فإن عاد الزوج فأكذب نفسه حده القاضي وحل له أن يتزوجها وكذلك إن قذف غيرها فحد أو زنت فحدت
cards.why: By admitting he lied he is punished for qadhf, and he may then marry her again.

cards.ask: In which of these does li'an take place, if the wife asks the judge?

options.text: He accuses his free Muslim wife, who has a clean record, of zina
He denies that his wife's newborn child is his
His wife is not a Muslim
His wife was once punished for qadhf herself
In al-Quduri's time, his wife was a slave woman

source: إذا قذف الرجل امرأته بالزنا وهما من أهل الشهادة والمرأة ممن يحد قاذفها أو نفى نسب ولدها
وهي أمة أو كافر أو محدودة في قذف
cards.why: Accusing a wife whose accuser would be punished, or denying her child, brings li'an. A non-Muslim wife, one punished for qadhf, or a slave wife brings no li'an.

lessons.title: Li'an: special cases and denying a child

cards.title: No li'an with these
cards.ar: وإذا قذف امرأته وهي صغيرة أو مجنونة فلا لعان بينهما وقذف الأخرس لا يتعلق به اللعان
cards.en: If he accuses his wife while she is a young girl or insane, there is no li'an between them. And when a mute man accuses (by signs), it does not lead to li'an.

cards.title: Words about a pregnancy
cards.ar: وإذا قال الزوج: ليس حملك مني فلا لعان بينهما وإن قال: زنيت وهذا الحمل من الزنا تلاعنا ولم ينف القاضي الحمل
cards.en: If the husband only says "Your pregnancy is not from me", there is no li'an. If he accuses her of zina and says the pregnancy is from it, they swear the li'an, but the judge does not cut off the unborn child's lineage.

cards.ask: Does this lead to li'an (if she asks the judge)?
items: He accuses her of zina and says her pregnancy is from it
He denies her baby right after the birth
He only says "Your pregnancy is not from me"
He accuses her while she is insane
A mute husband accuses her by signs
source: وإذا قذف امرأته وهي صغيرة أو مجنونة فلا لعان بينهما وقذف الأخرس لا يتعلق به اللعان وإذا قال الزوج: ليس حملك مني فلا لعان بينهما وإن قال: زنيت وهذا الحمل من الزنا تلاعنا
صح نفيه ولاعن به
cards.why: An open accusation tied to the pregnancy, or denying the newborn, brings li'an. "Not from me" alone, an insane wife, or a mute husband does not.

cards.title: Denying a newborn child
cards.ar: وإذا نفى الرجل ولد امرأته عقيب الولادة أو في الحال التي تقبل التهنئة أو تبتاع له آلة الولادة صح نفيه ولاعن به وإن نفاه بعد ذلك لاعن وثبت النسب
cards.en: If a man denies his wife's child right after the birth, or in the days when people congratulate and buy things for the baby, his denial is valid and the li'an is sworn over it. If he denies it later than that, li'an is sworn but the child's nasab (lineage) stays fixed to him.

cards.title: A different view on the time
cards.ar: وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: يصح نفيه في مدة النفاس
cards.en: Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say he may deny the child at any time during her nifas (the bleeding after childbirth).

cards.ask: Faris's son was born, and Faris accepted the congratulations of his family. Many months later he denies the child. What follows?
options: Li'an is sworn, but the boy stays his son
Li'an is sworn and the boy is joined to his mother only
cards.source: وإن نفاه بعد ذلك لاعن وثبت النسب
cards.why: A denial after the time of congratulations still brings li'an, but the child's lineage stays with the father.

cards.title: Twins
cards.ar: وإذا ولدت ولدين في بطن واحد فنفى الأول واعترف بالثاني ثبت نسبهما وحد الزوج وإن اعترف بالأول ونفى الثاني ثبت نسبهما ولاعن
cards.en: If she has twins and he denies the first but accepts the second, both are his, and he is punished for qadhf. If he accepts the first and denies the second, both are his, and li'an is sworn.

cards.ask: Adam's wife has twins. He denies the first-born, then accepts the second. What follows?
options: Both are his, and he is punished for qadhf
Both are his, and li'an is sworn
cards.source: فنفى الأول واعترف بالثاني ثبت نسبهما وحد الزوج
cards.why: Twins share one lineage, so both are his. Accepting the second after denying the first means he is punished for his accusation.

cards.ask: Yahya's wife has twins. He accepts the first, then denies the second. What follows?
options: Both are his, and li'an is sworn
Both are his, and he is punished for qadhf
cards.source: وإن اعترف بالأول ونفى الثاني ثبت نسبهما ولاعن
cards.why: Both are his because they are twins, and since the denial came last, li'an is sworn.

cards.title: Three periods
cards.ar: إذا طلق الرجل امرأته طلاقا بائنا أو رجعيا أو وقعت الفرقة بينهما بغير طلاق وهي حرة ممن تحيض فعدتها ثلاثة أقراء والأقراء: الحيض
cards.en: The 'idda is the waiting time after a marriage ends, before a woman may marry again. A divorce may be raj'i (he can take her back during the 'idda) or ba'in (final). After either, or after a separation that is not a divorce, a free woman who has periods waits three qur', and qur' here means monthly periods.

cards.title: No periods, or pregnant
cards.ar: وإن كانت لا تحيض من صغر أو كبر فعدتها ثلاثة أشهر وإن كانت حاملا فعدتها أن تضع حملها
cards.en: If she has no periods, because she is too young or past that age, her 'idda is three months. If she is pregnant, her 'idda ends when she gives birth.

cards.ask: Amina, aged 60, no longer has periods. Her husband divorces her. How long is her 'idda?
cards.source: وإن كانت لا تحيض من صغر أو كبر فعدتها ثلاثة أشهر
cards.why: A woman who has no periods because of her age waits three months.

cards.title: In al-Quduri's time: a slave woman
cards.ar: وإن كانت أمة فعدتها حيضتان وإن كانت لا تحيض فعدتها شهر ونصف
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, a married slave woman's 'idda was two periods, or a month and a half if she had no periods.

cards.title: When the husband dies
cards.ar: وإذا مات الرجل عن امرأته الحرة فعدتها أربعة أشهر وعشر وإن كانت أمة فعدتها شهران وخمسة أيام وإن كانت حاملا فعدتها أن تضع حملها
cards.en: When a husband dies, his free wife's 'idda is four months and ten days (a slave wife's, in al-Quduri's time, was two months and five days). If she is pregnant, her 'idda ends when she gives birth.

cards.ask: How long is this free woman's 'idda?
items: Separated without a divorce, and she has periods
Divorced, and too young for periods
Divorced, and past the age of periods
source: وهي حرة ممن تحيض فعدتها ثلاثة أقراء والأقراء: الحيض
فعدتها ثلاثة أشهر
وإذا مات الرجل عن امرأته الحرة فعدتها أربعة أشهر وعشر
cards.why: Divorce or separation with periods: three periods. No periods: three months. Widowhood: four months and ten days.

cards.ask: Sumayya's husband dies while she is pregnant. Three weeks later she gives birth. Is her 'idda over?
options: Yes: a pregnant woman's 'idda ends with the birth
No: she must still complete four months and ten days
No: she must wait three periods after the birth
cards.source: وإن كانت حاملا فعدتها أن تضع حملها وإذا ورثت
cards.why: For a pregnant widow, the 'idda ends when she gives birth, even if that is soon after the death.

cards.title: Divorced in his final illness
cards.ar: وإذا ورثت المطلقة في المرض فعدتها أبعد الأجلين
cards.en: If a man divorces his wife during his final illness and she still inherits from him, her 'idda is the longer of the two: the 'idda of divorce or the 'idda of death.

cards.ask: Ruqayya, who has periods, is divorced. What does 'three qur'' mean for her 'idda?
cards.source: فعدتها ثلاثة أقراء والأقراء: الحيض
cards.why: The book explains that the qur' are the periods, so she waits three periods.

cards.title: In al-Quduri's time: freed during the 'idda
cards.ar: فإن أعتقت الأمة في عدتها من طلاق رجعي انتقلت عدتها إلى عدة الحرائر وإن أعتقت وهي مبتوتة أو متوفى عنه زوجها لم تنتقل عدتها
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, if a slave woman was freed during the 'idda of a raj'i divorce, her 'idda changed to that of a free woman. If she was freed after a final divorce (mabtuta), or after her husband's death, her 'idda stayed as it was.

cards.title: If the periods come back
cards.ar: وإن كانت آيسة فاعتدت بالشهور ثم رأت الدم انتقض ما مضى من عدتها وكان عليها أن تستأنف العدة بالحيض
cards.en: If a woman past the age of periods (aysa) was counting her 'idda in months, and then she sees blood again, what has passed is cancelled. She must start her 'idda again, counting by periods.

cards.ask: Khadija, aged 56, had no periods and began a three-month 'idda. In the second month her periods return. What now?
options: She starts again and counts three periods
cards.source: ثم رأت الدم انتقض ما مضى من عدتها وكان عليها أن تستأنف العدة بالحيض
cards.why: Seeing blood again cancels the months already counted; she starts again by periods.

cards.title: A broken marriage, or a mistake
cards.ar: والمنكوحة نكاحا فاسدا والموطوءة بشبهة عدتها الحيض
cards.en: A woman in an invalid (fasid) marriage, or one who was with a man by honest mistake (shubha), counts her 'idda by periods, both when they separate and when he dies.

cards.title: In al-Quduri's time: an umm walad
cards.ar: أو أعتقها فعدتها ثلاث حيض
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, an umm walad (a slave woman who had borne her owner a child) waited three periods when her owner died or freed her.

cards.title: When a young husband dies
cards.ar: وإذا مات الصغير عن امرأته وبها حبل فعدتها أن تضع حملها وإن حدث الحبل بعد الموت فعدتها أربعة أشهر وعشر
cards.en: If a young boy who was married dies and his wife is pregnant, her 'idda ends with the birth. If the pregnancy began after his death, her 'idda is four months and ten days.

cards.ask: A young husband dies. His wife is found to be pregnant only after his death, the pregnancy having begun after it. What is her 'idda?
cards.source: وإن حدث الحبل بعد الموت فعدتها أربعة أشهر وعشر
cards.why: A pregnancy that began after the death does not end the 'idda; she waits four months and ten days.

cards.ask: Which of these women count their 'idda by periods?

options.text: A woman whose fasid marriage has been ended
A woman with periods who was with a man by honest mistake
An older woman whose periods came back during her 'idda in months
In al-Quduri's time, an umm walad freed by her owner
A free widow who is not pregnant

source: والمنكوحة نكاحا فاسدا والموطوءة بشبهة عدتها الحيض
وكان عليها أن تستأنف العدة بالحيض
أو أعتقها فعدتها ثلاث حيض
فعدتها أربعة أشهر وعشر
cards.why: The fasid marriage, the honest mistake, the returned periods and the freed umm walad all count periods. A free widow waits four months and ten days.

lessons.title: When the 'idda starts, and two at once

cards.title: Divorced during a period
cards.ar: وإذا طلق الرجل امرأته في حال الحيض لم تعتد بالحيضة التي وقع فيها الطلاق
cards.en: If a man divorces his wife while she is in her period, that period does not count towards her three.

cards.ask: Salma is divorced on the second day of her period. How many more complete periods must she wait after this one?
cards.source: لم تعتد بالحيضة التي وقع فيها الطلاق
cards.why: The period in which the divorce happened is not counted, so she waits three full periods after it.

cards.title: Two 'iddas overlap
cards.ar: وإذا وطئت المعتدة بشبهة فعليها عدة أخرى وتداخلت العدتان فيكون ما تراه من الحيض محتسبا به منهما جميعا وإذا انقضت العدة الأولى ولم تكمل الثانية فإن عليها تمام العدة الثانية
cards.en: If a woman in her 'idda is with a man by honest mistake, she owes a second 'idda. The two overlap: each period counts for both. When the first is over and the second is not, she completes the second.

cards.ask: A woman in 'idda has seen one period when a second 'idda (of three periods) becomes due by honest mistake. How many more periods must she wait in all?
cards.source: فيكون ما تراه من الحيض محتسبا به منهما جميعا وإذا انقضت العدة الأولى ولم تكمل الثانية فإن عليها تمام العدة الثانية
cards.why: Each new period counts for both. After two more the first is over, and one more completes the second: three in all.

cards.title: When the 'idda starts
cards.ar: وابتداء العدة في الطلاق عقيب الطلاق وفي الوفاة عقيب الوفاة فإن لم تعلم بالطلاق أو الوفاة حتى مضت مدة العدة فقد انقضت عدتها
cards.en: The 'idda of divorce starts right after the divorce, and the 'idda of death right after the death. If she does not learn of it until the whole time has passed, her 'idda is already over.

cards.ask: Hind's husband died while travelling far away. The news reaches her five months later. What is her 'idda now?
options: Four months and ten days from today
cards.source: فإن لم تعلم بالطلاق أو الوفاة حتى مضت مدة العدة فقد انقضت عدتها
cards.why: The 'idda starts at the death, not at the news. Four months and ten days have already passed, so it is over.

cards.title: Start of the 'idda in a fasid marriage
cards.ar: والعدة في النكاح الفاسد عقيب التفريق بينهما أو عزم الواطئ على ترك وطئها
cards.en: In an invalid (fasid) marriage, the 'idda starts once they are separated, or once the man makes up his mind to leave her.

cards.ask: When does the 'idda of death start? Complete it.
cards.ar: وفي الوفاة ____ الوفاة
cards.source: وفي الوفاة عقيب الوفاة
cards.why: عقيب: the 'idda of death begins straight after the death.

cards.ask: Layla's husband divorces her, but she only hears of it a month later. When did her 'idda start?
options: At the start of her next period
cards.source: وابتداء العدة في الطلاق عقيب الطلاق
cards.why: The 'idda of divorce starts right after the divorce, whether or not she knew of it.

cards.title: Ihdad: setting adornment aside
cards.ar: وعلى المبتوتة والمتوفى عنها زوجها - إذا كانت بالغة مسلمة - الإحداد وهو: ترك الطيب والزينة والدهن والكحل إلا من عذر ولا تختضب بالحناء ولا تلبس ثوبا مصبوغا بعصفر ولا بزعفران
cards.en: A woman in the 'idda of a final divorce, or a widow, if she is an adult Muslim, must keep ihdad (mourning). That means leaving perfume, adornment, oil and kohl (eye make-up), unless she needs them for a reason like illness. She does not use henna and does not wear clothes dyed with safflower or saffron.

cards.ask: During ihdad, what does the woman leave aside?

options.text: Perfume
Kohl, unless she needs it as treatment
Henna
Clothes dyed with saffron
Plain everyday clothes

cards.source: ترك الطيب والزينة والدهن والكحل إلا من عذر ولا تختضب بالحناء ولا تلبس ثوبا مصبوغا بعصفر ولا بزعفران
cards.why: Perfume, kohl (unless needed), henna and dyed clothes are left aside. Plain clothes are not forbidden.

cards.title: Who keeps ihdad
cards.ar: ولا إحداد على كافرة ولا صغيرة وعلى الأمة الإحداد وليس في عدة النكاح الفاسد ولا في عدة أم الولد إحداد
cards.en: There is no ihdad for a non-Muslim woman or a young girl. In al-Quduri's time a slave woman did keep it. There is no ihdad in the 'idda of a fasid marriage, nor in the 'idda of an umm walad.

cards.ask: Must she keep ihdad?
items: An adult Muslim woman after a final divorce
A young girl who is widowed
A woman whose fasid marriage was ended
source: وعلى المبتوتة والمتوفى عنها زوجها - إذا كانت بالغة مسلمة - الإحداد
ولا إحداد على كافرة ولا صغيرة
وليس في عدة النكاح الفاسد
cards.why: Adult Muslim widows and finally divorced women keep ihdad; a non-Muslim, a young girl and the fasid marriage have none.

cards.title: Proposals during the 'idda
cards.ar: ولا ينبغي أن تخطب المعتدة ولا بأس بالتعريض في الخطبة
cards.en: A woman in her 'idda should not be proposed to openly. But there is no harm in hinting at a proposal.

cards.ask: Sana is in her 'idda after her husband died. Yusuf wishes to marry her. What may he do now?
options: Only hint that he is interested
cards.source: ولا ينبغي أن تخطب المعتدة ولا بأس بالتعريض في الخطبة
cards.why: Open proposals are not proper during the 'idda, but a hint is fine.

cards.title: Leaving the house
cards.ar: ولا يجوز للمطلقة الرجعية والمبتوتة الخروج من بيتها ليلا ولا نهارا والمتوفى عنها زوجها تخرج نهارا وبعض الليل ولا تبيت في غير منزلها
cards.en: A divorced woman in her 'idda, raj'i or final, may not leave her home by night or by day. A widow may go out by day and part of the night, but she does not spend the night anywhere but her home.

cards.ask: Maryam is a widow in her 'idda. She wants to go out in the day to work and return home in the evening. Is this allowed?
options: Yes: a widow may go out by day, as long as she sleeps at home
No: she may not leave at all
Yes, and she may also stay overnight with her sister
cards.source: والمتوفى عنها زوجها تخرج نهارا وبعض الليل ولا تبيت في غير منزلها
cards.why: A widow may go out by day and part of the night, but she spends the night at home.

cards.title: Which home
cards.ar: وعلى المعتدة أن تعتد في المنزل الذي يضاف إليها بالسكنى حال وقوع الفرقة فإن كان نصيبها من دار الميت لا يكفيها وأخرجها الورثة من نصيبهم انتقلت
cards.en: She spends her 'idda in the home she was living in when the marriage ended. If her share of her late husband's house is too small for her and the other heirs move her out of their shares, she moves. And a husband may not take his wife on a journey during a raj'i 'idda.

cards.title: Remarrying her during her 'idda
cards.ar: وإذا طلق الرجل امرأته طلاقا بائنا ثم تزوجها في عدتها وطلقها قبل أن يدخل بها فعليه مهر كامل وعليها عدة مستقبلة وقال محمد: لها نصف المهر وعليها إتمام العدة الأولى
cards.en: If a man gives his wife a ba'in divorce, marries her again during her 'idda, and divorces her before they are together, he owes a full mahr (the marriage gift) and she starts a new 'idda. Note: Muhammad says she gets half the mahr and only completes the first 'idda.

cards.ask: Which of these are right for a woman in her 'idda?

options.text: A raj'i divorcee stays in her home by night and day
A man may hint that he would like to marry her
Her husband may not take her travelling during a raj'i 'idda
A widow may spend nights at her sister's house
She may be openly proposed to

source: ولا يجوز للمطلقة الرجعية والمبتوتة الخروج من بيتها ليلا ولا نهارا
ولا بأس بالتعريض في الخطبة
ولا يجوز أن يسافر الزوج بالمطلقة الرجعية
ولا تبيت في غير منزلها
cards.why: She stays at home, a hint is allowed, and no journey with the husband in a raj'i 'idda. A widow sleeps at home, and open proposals are not proper.

lessons.title: A child born during or after the 'idda

cards.title: After a raj'i divorce
cards.ar: ويثبت نسب ولد المطلقة الرجعية إذا جاءت به لسنتين أو أكثر ما لم تقر بانقضاء عدتها
cards.en: Nasab is a child's lineage: being known as the father's child. After a raj'i divorce, her child is joined to the husband even if born two years or more later, as long as she has not said her 'idda is over.

cards.title: Less or more than two years
cards.ar: لأقل من سنتين بانت من زوجها وإن جاءت به لأكثر من سنتين ثبت نسبه وكانت رجعة
cards.en: If the child comes in less than two years, she has become separated from him (the pregnancy was before the divorce, so her 'idda ended with the birth). If it comes after more than two years, the child is his and this counts as his taking her back (raj'a).

cards.ask: Ahmad gave his wife a raj'i divorce. She never said her 'idda was over, and gives birth two and a half years later. What follows?
options: The child is his, and it counts as him taking her back
The child is his, and she is now fully separated
cards.source: وإن جاءت به لأكثر من سنتين ثبت نسبه وكانت رجعة
cards.why: After more than two years the child is his and he is taken to have resumed the marriage.

cards.title: After a final divorce
cards.ar: والمبتوتة يثبت نسب ولدها إذا جاءت به لأقل من سنتين فإن جاءت به لتمام سنتين من يوم الفرقة لم يثبت نسبه إلا أن يدعيه
cards.en: After a final divorce, her child is his if born within less than two years. If it is born two full years after the separation, it is not joined to him, unless he claims it.

cards.title: After the husband's death
cards.ar: ويثبت نسب ولد المتوفى عنها زوجها ما بين الوفاة وبين سنتين
cards.en: A widow's child is joined to her late husband if born between his death and two years after it.

cards.ask: Asma's husband died. She has not said her 'idda is over, and gives birth 18 months after his death. Is the child his?
options: Yes: it is within two years of the death
No: it is after four months and ten days
Only if two witnesses saw the marriage
cards.source: ما بين الوفاة وبين سنتين
cards.why: A child born between the death and two years after it is joined to the late husband.

cards.title: After she says her 'idda is over
cards.ar: وإذا اعترفت المعتدة بانقضاء عدتها ثم جاءت بولد لأقل من ستة أشهر ثبت نسبه وإن جاءت به لستة أشهر لم يثبت نسبه
cards.en: If she says her 'idda is over and then gives birth less than six months later, the child is his (she must already have been pregnant). If it is six months or more later, it is not joined to him.

cards.ask: Zaynab told the judge her 'idda was over. Four months later she gives birth. Is the child her former husband's?
options: Yes: it is less than six months
No: she said her 'idda was over
Only if he claims the child
cards.source: ثم جاءت بولد لأقل من ستة أشهر ثبت نسبه
cards.why: Less than six months after she said her 'idda ended, so she was already pregnant and the child is his.

cards.ask: After a final divorce, a woman gives birth exactly two years from the day of the separation, and the man does not claim the child. Is the child joined to him?
cards.source: فإن جاءت به لتمام سنتين من يوم الفرقة لم يثبت نسبه
cards.why: After a final divorce the child must come in less than two years; at a full two years it is not joined to him unless he claims it.

lessons.title: Proving a birth, and the length of pregnancy

cards.title: Proving a birth in the 'idda
cards.ar: وإذا ولدت المعتدة ولدا لم يثبت نسبه عند أبي حنيفة إلا أن يشهد بولادتها رجلان أول رجل وامرأتان إلا أن يكون هناك حبل ظاهر أو اعتراف من قبل الزوج فيثبت النسب من غير شهادة
cards.en: If a woman in her 'idda gives birth (and the husband denies the birth), the child is joined to him, according to Abu Hanifa, only when two men, or one man and two women, testify to the birth. But if her pregnancy was plain to see, or the husband admitted it, no witnesses are needed.

cards.title: A different view
cards.ar: وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: يثبت في الجميع بشهادة امرأة واحدة
cards.en: Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say that in every case, the testimony of one woman is enough.

cards.ask: Nur's pregnancy was clear for all to see during her 'idda. She gives birth, and her former husband says the birth never happened. Does she need witnesses?
options: No: a plain pregnancy fixes the lineage without witnesses
Yes, one man and two women
cards.source: إلا أن يكون هناك حبل ظاهر أو اعتراف من قبل الزوج فيثبت النسب من غير شهادة
cards.why: When the pregnancy was plain, or the husband admitted it, the lineage is fixed without any testimony.

cards.title: Born soon after the wedding
cards.ar: وإذا تزوج امرأة فجاءت بولد لأقل من ستة أشهر منذ يوم تزوجها لم يثبت نسبه وإن جاءت به لستة أشهر فصاعدا ثبت إن اعترف به الزوج أو سكت وإن جحد الولادة ثبت بشهادة امرأة واحدة تشهد بالولادة
cards.en: If a man marries a woman and she gives birth less than six months after the wedding, the child is not joined to him. At six months or more, the child is his if he accepts it or stays silent. If he denies the birth itself, it is proven by one woman's testimony.

cards.ask: Hamza and Ruqayya married seven months ago. She gives birth, and Hamza says nothing either way. Is the child his?
options: Yes: six months or more, and he was silent
No: he must say it out loud
No: it must be nine months
cards.source: وإن جاءت به لستة أشهر فصاعدا ثبت إن اعترف به الزوج أو سكت
cards.why: At six months or more after the wedding, the child is his if he admits it or stays silent.

cards.title: Shortest and longest pregnancy
cards.ar: وأكثر مدة الحمل سنتان وأقله ستة أشهر
cards.en: The longest a pregnancy is counted is two years, and the shortest is six months. This is why the book keeps using these two numbers.

cards.ask: What is the shortest pregnancy? Complete it.
cards.ar: وأكثر مدة الحمل سنتان وأقله ____
cards.source: وأكثر مدة الحمل سنتان وأقله ستة أشهر
cards.why: ستة أشهر: the shortest pregnancy is six months, and the longest two years.

cards.title: Two last rules
cards.ar: وإذا طلق الذمي الذمية فلا عدة عليها وإذا تزوجت الحامل من الزنا جاز النكاح ولا يطؤها حتى تضع حملها
cards.en: If a dhimmi (a non-Muslim living under Muslim rule) divorces his dhimmi wife, she has no 'idda. And if a woman pregnant from zina marries, the nikah is valid, but the husband does not live with her as a wife until she gives birth.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: The longest pregnancy is two years
A dhimmi woman divorced by a dhimmi has no 'idda
A child born four months after the wedding is not joined to the husband
A woman pregnant from zina cannot be married at all
The shortest pregnancy is nine months

source: وأكثر مدة الحمل سنتان وأقله ستة أشهر
وإذا طلق الذمي الذمية فلا عدة عليها
لأقل من ستة أشهر منذ يوم تزوجها لم يثبت نسبه
وإذا تزوجت الحامل من الزنا جاز النكاح
cards.why: Two years at most and six months at least; no 'idda between dhimmis; under six months the child is not his. Her nikah is valid, but he waits until the birth.

cards.title: Food, clothing and a home
cards.ar: النفقة واجبة على زوجها مسلمة كانت أو كافرة
cards.en: Nafaqa (maintenance) is what a husband must provide for his wife: her food, her clothing and her home. It is due to her whether she is Muslim or not, once she has come to live in his home.

cards.title: Measured by them both
cards.ar: فعليه نفقتها وكسوتها وسكناها يعتبر ذلك لحالهما جميعا موسرا كان الزوج أو معسرا
cards.en: He owes her food, clothing and housing. How much is judged by the situation of both of them together, whether the husband is well off (musir) or short of money (mu'sir).

cards.ask: What does the husband owe his wife? Complete it.
cards.ar: فعليه نفقتها وكسوتها ____
cards.source: فعليه نفقتها وكسوتها وسكناها
cards.why: وسكناها: he owes her food, clothing and a home to live in.

cards.title: Waiting for the mahr, or leaving his home
cards.ar: فإن امتنعت من تسليم نفسها حتى يعطيها مهرها فلها النفقة وإن نشزت
cards.en: If she will not move to his home until he gives her the mahr (the marriage gift owed to her), she still gets maintenance, because she has that right. But if she becomes nashiza (leaves his home in defiance, without a right), she has no maintenance until she comes back.

cards.ask: Fatima's nikah is done, but she will not move into her husband's home until he pays the mahr due to her. Does she get maintenance meanwhile?
options: Yes: she is holding back for her right
No: she has not moved in
cards.source: فإن امتنعت من تسليم نفسها حتى يعطيها مهرها فلها النفقة
cards.why: Waiting for the mahr that is owed to her does not take away her maintenance.

cards.title: When one of them is young
cards.ar: وإن كانت صغيرة لا يستمتع بها فلا نفقة لها وإن سلمت نفسها إليه وإن كان الزوج صغيرا لا يقدر على الوطء والمرأة كبيرة فلها النفقة من ماله
cards.en: If the wife is still a young girl, too young for married life, she has no maintenance even if she is handed over to him. If the husband is a young boy, too young for married life, and the wife is grown up, she gets maintenance from his wealth.

cards.title: Divorce and death
cards.ar: وإذا طلق الرجل امرأته فلها النفقة والسكنى في عدتها رجعيا كان أو بائنا ولا نفقة للمتوفى عنها زوجها
cards.en: If a man divorces his wife, she gets maintenance and a home during her 'idda (the waiting time after divorce), whether the divorce is raj'i or ba'in. A widow gets no maintenance.

cards.title: When the separation is her wrongdoing
cards.ar: وكل فرقة جاءت من قبل المرأة بمعصية فلا نفقة لها وإن طلقها ثم ارتدت سقطت نفقتها وإن أمكنت ابن زوجها من نفسها إن كان بعد الطلاق فلها النفقة وإن كان قبل الطلاق فلا نفقة لها
cards.en: Any separation that comes from the wife by a sin leaves her no maintenance. If he divorced her and she then leaves Islam, her maintenance ends. Likewise, if she wrongly allows her husband's son to be intimate with her: if this is after the divorce she keeps her maintenance, but if it is before, she has none.

cards.title: Away from home, or ill
cards.ar: وإذا حبست المرأة في دين أو غصبها رجل كرها فذهب بها أو حجت مع محرم فلا نفقة لها وإن مرضت في منزل الزوج فلها النفقة
cards.en: If she is held in prison for a debt, or a man takes her away by force, or she goes for Hajj with a mahram (a close relative she may not marry), she has no maintenance for that time. If she falls ill in her husband's home, she still gets it.

cards.ask: Does the wife get maintenance?
items: She is in her 'idda after a ba'in divorce
Her young husband cannot yet live with her, but she is grown up
She left his home in defiance and has not returned
She has gone for Hajj with her brother
source: وإن مرضت في منزل الزوج فلها النفقة
فلها النفقة والسكنى في عدتها رجعيا كان أو بائنا
فلها النفقة من ماله
نفقة لها حتى تعود إلى منزله
أو حجت مع محرم فلا نفقة لها
ولا نفقة للمتوفى عنها زوجها
cards.why: Illness at home, the 'idda of divorce and a young husband keep her maintenance. Leaving in defiance, Hajj with a mahram and widowhood do not.

cards.ask: After a quarrel, Huda leaves her husband's home without any right to, and stays away for two months. Does she get maintenance for those months?
options: No, not until she returns to his home
Yes: she is still his wife
cards.source: نفقة لها حتى تعود إلى منزله
cards.why: A wife who leaves in defiance has no maintenance until she returns to his home.

cards.ask: Sakina was divorced with a raj'i divorce. During her 'idda she leaves Islam. What happens to her maintenance?
cards.source: وإن طلقها ثم ارتدت سقطت نفقتها
cards.why: Leaving Islam after the divorce ends her maintenance, because the cause comes from her own wrongdoing.

lessons.title: Her servant, her home and her family
lessons.arabic: وعليه أن يسكنها في دار منفردة

cards.title: A servant
cards.ar: وتفرض على الزوج نفقة خادمها إذا كان موسرا ولا تفرض لأكثر من خادم واحد
cards.en: If the husband is well off, he must also pay for her servant's keep. But he is not made to pay for more than one servant.

cards.ask: Umar is wealthy. His wife has three servants and asks the judge to make him pay for all of them. What does the judge order?
options: The keep of one servant only
None: servants are her own affair
cards.source: وتفرض على الزوج نفقة خادمها إذا كان موسرا ولا تفرض لأكثر من خادم واحد
cards.why: A wealthy husband pays for her servant, but never for more than one.

cards.title: A home of her own
cards.ar: وعليه أن يسكنها في دار منفردة ليس فيها أحد من أهله إلا أن تختار ذلك وإن كان له ولد من غيرها فليس له أن يسكنه معها
cards.en: He must give her a home of her own, with none of his relatives living in it, unless she chooses that. If he has a child from another wife, he may not make that child live with her.

cards.title: Her parents and family
cards.ar: للزوج أن يمنع والديها وولدها من غيره وأهلها من الدخول عليها ولا يمنعهم من النظر إليها وكلامها أي وقت اختاروا
cards.en: The husband may stop her parents, her child from another husband, and her relatives from coming into the home. But he may not stop them from seeing her and speaking with her, at any time they choose.

cards.ask: Which of these are right about the wife's home?

options.text: She may refuse to share the house with his relatives
He may not make his son from another wife live with her
He may not stop her parents seeing and speaking with her
He may stop her parents from ever speaking with her
She must live with his family if he wishes

source: في دار منفردة ليس فيها أحد من أهله إلا أن تختار ذلك
وإن كان له ولد من غيرها فليس له أن يسكنه معها
ولا يمنعهم من النظر إليها وكلامها أي وقت اختاروا
cards.why: She has the right to a home without his relatives, unless she chooses otherwise, and without his child from another wife. Her family may always see her and speak with her.

cards.title: When he cannot pay
cards.ar: ومن أعسر بنفقة امرأته لم يفرق بينهما ويقال لها: استديني عليه
cards.en: If a husband cannot afford his wife's maintenance, they are not separated for that. She is told: borrow, and it becomes his debt.

cards.ask: Bilal has lost his work and cannot pay his wife's maintenance. She asks the judge to end the marriage. What does the judge do?
options: He does not separate them; she borrows, and it is Bilal's debt
He cancels Bilal's duty to pay
cards.source: ومن أعسر بنفقة امرأته لم يفرق بينهما ويقال لها: استديني عليه
cards.why: Being unable to pay is no reason to separate them. She borrows, and the debt is on him.

cards.ask: Rashid is poor and does not have a servant to pay for. His wife says he must pay for one. Must he?
options: No: a servant's keep is due only from a well-off husband
cards.source: وتفرض على الزوج نفقة خادمها إذا كان موسرا
cards.why: The servant's keep is ordered only when the husband is well off.

lessons.title: When maintenance is owed or missed

cards.title: An absent husband
cards.ar: وإذا غاب الرجل وله مال في يد رجل وهو يعرف به وبالزوجية فرض القاضي في ذلك المال نفقة زوجة الغائب وأولاده الصغار ووالديه ويأخذ منها كفيلا بها ولا يقضى بنفقة في مال الغائب إلا لهؤلاء
cards.en: If a husband is away and someone holds his money, and that person admits it and admits the marriage, the judge orders maintenance from that money for his wife, his young children and his parents. He takes a guarantor (kafil) from her. No one else is given maintenance from an absent man's money.

cards.ask: Yasin is abroad. His friend holds his money and admits both the money and the marriage. Who can the judge give maintenance to from it?
options: His wife, his young children and his parents
Anyone in his family who is poor
cards.source: فرض القاضي في ذلك المال نفقة زوجة الغائب وأولاده الصغار ووالديه
cards.why: From an absent man's money, maintenance is ordered only for his wife, his young children and his parents.

cards.title: If he becomes richer
cards.ar: وإذا قضى القاضي لها بنفقة الإعسار ثم أيسر فخاصمته تمم لها نفقة الموسر
cards.en: If the judge set her maintenance at the level of a poor man, and the husband then becomes well off, and she takes it to the judge, he raises it to the level of a well-off man.

cards.title: Months that went unpaid
cards.ar: وإذا مضت مدة لم ينفق الزوج عليها وطالبته بذلك فلا شيء لها إلا أن يكون القاضي فرض لها النفقة أو صالحت الزوج على مقدارها
cards.en: If time passes and he does not maintain her, and she asks for it later, she gets nothing for the past, unless the judge had already set her maintenance, or she had agreed an amount with her husband. If he dies after the judge's order while months were still unpaid, that unpaid maintenance falls away.

cards.ask: Ayesha's husband gave her nothing for three months. No judge had set an amount and they had never agreed one. She now asks for the three months. What does she get?
cards.source: فلا شيء لها إلا أن يكون القاضي فرض لها النفقة أو صالحت الزوج على مقدارها
cards.why: Past maintenance is owed only if a judge set it or the couple agreed an amount. Neither happened here.

cards.title: Paid in advance, then he dies
cards.ar: وإن أسلفها نفقة سنة ثم مات
cards.en: If he paid her a year's maintenance in advance and then died, nothing is taken back from her. Note: Muhammad says she keeps only what covers the time that passed, and the rest goes back to the husband.

cards.title: In al-Quduri's time: an enslaved husband or wife
cards.ar: وإذا تزوج العبد حرة فنفقتها دين عليه يباع فيها وإذا تزوج الرجل أمة فبوأها مولاها معه منزلا فعليه النفقة وإن لم يبوئها فلا نفقة لها
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, if an enslaved man married a free woman, her maintenance was a debt on him, and he could be sold to pay it. If a man married a slave woman and her master gave her a home with her husband, he owed her maintenance; if not, he did not.

cards.ask: The judge set Mariam's maintenance at a poor man's level. Later her husband becomes rich, and she takes him back to the judge. What happens?
options: The judge raises it to a rich man's level
cards.source: ثم أيسر فخاصمته تمم لها نفقة الموسر
cards.why: Maintenance follows his means: when he becomes well off and she asks, it is raised to the level of a well-off man.

cards.title: The father alone
cards.ar: ونفقة الأولاد الصغار على الأب لا يشاركه فيها أحد كما لا يشاركه في نفقة الزوجة أحد
cards.en: The maintenance of young children is on their father, and no one shares it with him, just as no one shares with him the maintenance of his wife.

cards.title: Nursing the baby
cards.ar: فليس على أمه أن ترضعه ويستأجر له الأب من ترضعه عندها فإن استأجرها وهي زوجته أو معتدته لترضع ولدها لم يجز وإن انقضت عدتها فاستأجرها على إرضاعه جاز
cards.en: If the young child is a nursing baby, the mother is not made to nurse it. The father hires a woman to nurse it at the mother's side. If he hires the mother herself while she is his wife or in her 'idda from him, the hiring is not valid. Once her 'idda is over, he may hire her to nurse it.

cards.ask: Ali divorced Sumayya, and her 'idda is now over. He hires her for a wage to nurse their baby son. Is this hiring valid?
options: No: a mother can never be paid to nurse her own child
Only if no one else is available
cards.source: وإن انقضت عدتها فاستأجرها على إرضاعه جاز
cards.why: Once her 'idda is over, the father may hire her to nurse their child.

cards.title: The mother comes first
cards.ar: فإن قال الأب لا أستأجرها وجاء بغيرها فرضيت الأم بمثل أجر الأجنبية كانت الأم أحق به وإن التمست زيادة لم يجبر الزوج عليها
cards.en: If the father says, "I will not hire her," and brings another woman, but the mother is happy with the same wage as the stranger, the mother has more right to nurse the baby. If she asks for more, the father is not forced to pay it.

cards.ask: A father finds a nurse who will take 100 dirhams. The baby's mother, whose 'idda is over, offers to nurse for the same 100. Who has more right?
cards.source: فرضيت الأم بمثل أجر الأجنبية كانت الأم أحق به
cards.why: When the mother accepts the same wage as the stranger, she has more right to nurse her child.

cards.title: Even if their religion differs
cards.ar: ونفقة الصغير واجبة على أبيه وإن خالفه في دينه كما تجب نفقة الزوجة على الزوج وإن خالفته في دينه
cards.en: A young child's maintenance is due from the father even if their religion differs, just as a wife's maintenance is due from her husband even if her religion is different from his.

cards.ask: Which of these are right about a young child's maintenance and nursing?

options.text: The father pays it alone
The father must pay even if the child's religion differs from his
The mother is not forced to nurse the baby
The mother's family shares the cost
He may validly hire his own wife to nurse their baby

source: ونفقة الأولاد الصغار على الأب لا يشاركه فيها أحد
ونفقة الصغير واجبة على أبيه وإن خالفه في دينه
فليس على أمه أن ترضعه
فإن استأجرها وهي زوجته أو معتدته لترضع ولدها لم يجز
cards.why: The father alone pays, whatever the child's religion, and the mother is not forced to nurse. Hiring his own wife for it is not valid.

cards.ask: A divorced mother whose 'idda is over offers to nurse the baby, but asks for more than the nurse the father found. Must the father pay her higher wage?
options: No, he is not forced to
Yes: the mother always has more right
Yes, but only half of the extra
cards.source: وإن التمست زيادة لم يجبر الزوج عليها
cards.why: The mother comes first only at the same wage. If she asks for more, he is not forced to pay it.

cards.title: The mother has the most right
cards.ar: كتاب الحضانة وإذا وقعت الفرقة بين الزوجين فالأم أحق بالولد فإن لم تكن الأم فأم الأم أولى من أم الأب
cards.en: Hadana is the right to bring up and look after a young child. When husband and wife separate, the mother has the most right to the child. If there is no mother, the mother's mother comes before the father's mother.

cards.title: Who comes next
cards.ar: فإن لم تكن فأم الأب أولى من الأخوات فإن لم تكن جدة فلأخوات أولى من العمات والخالات وتقدم الأخت من الأب والأم ثم الأخت من الأم ثم الأخت من الأب ثم الخالات أولى من العمات
cards.en: After the grandmothers come the child's sisters, who come before aunts: first a full sister, then a sister through the mother, then a sister through the father. Then the mother's sisters (khalat), who come before the father's sisters ('ammat), each in the same order.

cards.ask: Put these in the order of their right to bring up the child.
source: فالأم أحق بالولد فإن لم تكن الأم فأم الأم أولى من أم الأب
وتقدم الأخت من الأب والأم ثم الأخت من الأم ثم الأخت من الأب ثم الخالات أولى من العمات وينزلن كذلك ثم العمات ينزلن كذلك
cards.why: Mother, then her mother, then the father's mother, then sisters (full, through the mother, through the father), then the mother's sisters, then the father's sisters.

cards.title: If she marries
cards.ar: وكل من تزوجت من هؤلاء سقط حقها إلا الجدة إذا كان زوجها الجد وإن لم تكن للصبي امرأة من أهله واختصم فيه الرجال فأولاهم به أقربهم تعصبيا
cards.en: Any of these women who marries loses her right, except a grandmother married to the child's grandfather. If the child has no woman in the family and the men dispute over him, the one with most right is the closest relative through the father's line.

cards.ask: After the divorce, little Hasan lives with his mother. She then marries another man. Hasan's mother's mother is alive. What happens to the mother's right?
options: It falls away, and her mother comes next
It passes to the father at once
source: وكل من تزوجت من هؤلاء سقط حقها
فإن لم تكن الأم فأم الأم أولى من أم الأب
cards.why: A woman who marries loses her right, so it moves on to the next in line: the mother's mother.

cards.title: Until what age
cards.ar: والأم والجدة أحق بالغلام حتى يأكل وحده ويلبس وحده ويستنجي وحده وبالجارية حتى تحيض ومن سوى الأم والجدة أحق بالجارية حتى تبلغ حدا تشتهى
cards.en: The mother and grandmother keep a boy until he can eat, dress and clean himself after the toilet on his own, and a girl until she reaches puberty. Other women keep a girl until she is old enough to be thought of for marriage.

cards.ask: Musa's son now eats, dresses and cleans himself all on his own. Until now the boy has lived with his divorced mother. Does her right over him continue?
options: No: her right lasts until he can do these things alone
Yes, until he is an adult
cards.source: والأم والجدة أحق بالغلام حتى يأكل وحده ويلبس وحده ويستنجي وحده
cards.why: The mother's right over a boy lasts until he can eat, dress and clean himself on his own.

cards.title: Other mothers
cards.ar: والأمة إذا أعتقها مولاها وأم الولد إذا أعتقت في الولد كالحرة وليس للأمة وأم الولد قبل العتق حق في الولد والذمية أحق بولدها المسلم ما لم يعقل الأديان ويخاف أن يألف الكفر
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, an enslaved mother had no right of hadana until she was freed; once freed she was like a free woman. A dhimmi mother (a non-Muslim living under Muslim rule) has more right to her Muslim child until the child understands religion and there is a fear it will grow used to disbelief.

cards.title: Taking the child away
cards.ar: وإذا أرادت المطلقة أن تخرج بولدها من المصر فليس لها ذلك إلا أن تخرجه إلى وطنها وقد كان الزوج تزوجها فيه
cards.en: A divorced mother may not take the child out of the city, unless she takes it to her home town where the husband had married her.

cards.ask: Aisha was married in her home town of Basra and moved with her husband to Kufa. After the divorce she wants to take her little daughter back to Basra. May she?
options: Yes: it is her home town where he married her
No: she may never leave the city with the child
cards.source: إلا أن تخرجه إلى وطنها وقد كان الزوج تزوجها فيه
cards.why: She may take the child to her home town if that is where the husband married her.

lessons.title: Parents and relatives
lessons.arabic: وعلى الرجل أن ينفق على أبويه

cards.title: Parents and grandparents
cards.ar: وعلى الرجل أن ينفق على أبويه وأجداده وجداته إذا كانوا فقراء وإن خالفوه في دينه
cards.en: A man must maintain his parents and grandparents if they are poor, even if their religion differs from his.

cards.title: Different religions
cards.ar: ولا تجب النفقة مع اختلاف الدين إلا للزوجة والأبوين والأجداد والجدات والولد وولد الولد ولا يشارك الولد في نفقة أبويه أحد
cards.en: When the religion differs, maintenance is due only to a wife, parents, grandparents, children and grandchildren. And no one shares with a child the maintenance of his parents.

cards.ask: Hamid is Muslim. Which of these poor relatives, who are not Muslim, must he still maintain?

options.text: His father
His grandmother
His young son
His brother
His uncle

source: ولا تجب النفقة مع اختلاف الدين إلا للزوجة والأبوين والأجداد والجدات والولد وولد الولد
ولا تجب نفقتهم مع اختلاف الدين
cards.why: With a different religion, only wife, parents, grandparents, children and grandchildren are owed maintenance. Brothers and uncles are not.

cards.title: Other close relatives
cards.ar: والنفقة لكل ذي رحم محرم إذا كان صغيرا فقيرا أو كانت امرأة بالغة فقيرة أو كان ذكرا زمنا أو أعمى فقيرا ويجب ذلك على مقدار الميراث
cards.en: Maintenance is also due to every close relative he may never marry (dhu rahim mahram), if the relative is a poor child, a poor grown woman, or a poor man who is chronically disabled or blind. It is shared out in the same proportions as inheritance.

cards.title: Father two-thirds, mother one-third
cards.ar: وتجب نفقة الابنة البالغة والابن الزمن على أبويه أثلاثا: على الأب الثلثان وعلى الأم الثلث
cards.en: A grown daughter, or a son who is chronically disabled, is maintained by both parents in thirds: two-thirds from the father and one-third from the mother.

cards.ask: Sara is grown up, unmarried and poor. Both her parents are alive and able. Her maintenance costs 300 dirhams a month. How much does her father pay?
cards.source: على الأب الثلثان وعلى الأم الثلث
cards.why: The father pays two-thirds (200) and the mother one-third (100).

cards.title: When it is not due
cards.ar: ولا تجب نفقتهم مع اختلاف الدين ولا تجب على الفقير
cards.en: These other relatives are not owed maintenance when the religion differs, and it is not due from someone who is poor.

cards.ask: Khalid's adult brother is blind and poor, and they share the same religion. Khalid is well off. Must he maintain his brother?
options: Yes: a poor, blind close relative is owed maintenance
No: only parents and children are owed it
cards.source: أو كان ذكرا زمنا أو أعمى فقيرا
cards.why: A brother is a close relative he may never marry, and a poor blind man is owed maintenance by such relatives.

lessons.title: An absent son's money, and those one owns

cards.title: An absent son's money
cards.ar: وإذا كان للابن الغائب مال فضي عليه بنفقة أبويه وإن باع أبوه متاعه في نفقته جاز عند أبي حنيفة وإن باع العقار لم يجز
cards.en: If a son is away and has money, the judge orders his parents' maintenance from it. If his father sells the son's goods (movable things) for his own keep, it is valid according to Abu Hanifa. If he sells the son's land or buildings, it is not valid.

cards.title: Who is holding the money
cards.ar: وإن كان للابن الغائب مال في يد أبويه فانفقا منه لم يضمنا وإن كان له مال في يد أجنبي فأنفق عليهما بغير إذن القاضي ضمن
cards.en: If the absent son's money is with his parents and they spend from it on themselves, they owe nothing back. If it is with a stranger who spends it on them without the judge's permission, the stranger must pay it back.

cards.ask: Idris is travelling. He left 1,000 dirhams with his poor parents, and they spend 200 on their food. Must they pay it back?
cards.source: وإن كان للابن الغائب مال في يد أبويه فانفقا منه لم يضمنا
cards.why: Parents who spend on themselves from their absent son's money in their own hands owe nothing.

cards.ask: Idris also left money with his neighbour Saleh. Without asking the judge, Saleh spends some of it on Idris's poor parents. What follows?
options: Nothing: it was spent on the parents
The parents must pay it back
cards.source: وإن كان له مال في يد أجنبي فأنفق عليهما بغير إذن القاضي ضمن
cards.why: A stranger who spends the money without the judge's permission must make it good.

cards.title: Unpaid months fall away
cards.ar: وإذا قضى القاضي للولد والوالدين وذوي الأرحام بالنفقة فمضت مدة سقطت إلا أن يأذن القاضي في الاستدانة عليه
cards.en: If the judge orders maintenance for children, parents or other relatives, and time passes without it being paid, it falls away, unless the judge allowed them to borrow against him.

cards.ask: The judge ordered Tahir to maintain his poor uncle, but did not let the uncle borrow against Tahir. Four months pass unpaid. Does Tahir owe the four months?
cards.source: فمضت مدة سقطت إلا أن يأذن القاضي في الاستدانة عليه
cards.why: The unpaid months fall away, because the judge had not allowed borrowing against him.

cards.title: In al-Quduri's time: those one owned
cards.ar: وعلى المولى أن ينفق على عبده وأمته فإن امتنع وكن لهما كسب اكتسبا وأنفقها على أنفسهما وإن لم يكن لهما كسب أجبر المولى على بيعهما
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, a master had to provide for the people he owned. If he refused and they could earn, they worked and spent on themselves. If they could not earn, the master was forced to sell them to someone who would provide for them.

cards.ask: Which of these are right?

options.text: The judge may order parents' maintenance from an absent son's money
A stranger who spends it without the judge's permission must repay it
In al-Quduri's time, a master who refused to provide could be forced to sell
Unpaid relatives' maintenance is always owed later
Parents who spend from their son's money in their hands must repay it

source: وإذا كان للابن الغائب مال فضي عليه بنفقة أبويه
فأنفق عليهما بغير إذن القاضي ضمن
أجبر المولى على بيعهما
فمضت مدة سقطت
فانفقا منه لم يضمنا
cards.why: Parents can be maintained from his money, a stranger without permission repays, and a master who would not provide was forced to sell. Unpaid months fall away, and parents holding the money owe nothing.

cards.title: Three kinds
cards.ar: الأيمان على ثلاثة أضرب: يمين غموس ويمين منعقدة ويمين لغو
cards.en: An oath (yamin) is when you swear, for example "By Allah, I will...". Al-Quduri says there are three kinds: the ghamus oath, the mun'aqida (binding) oath and the laghw (slip) oath.

cards.title: The ghamus oath
cards.ar: فاليمين الغموس هي: الحلف على أمر ماض يتعمد الكذب فيه فهذه اليمين يأثم بها صاحبها ولا كفارة فيها إلا الاستغفار
cards.en: The ghamus oath is swearing about something in the past while lying on purpose. The person sins. There is no kaffara for it (a kaffara is an act, like feeding the poor, that makes up for a broken oath). The only way out is istighfar: asking Allah's forgiveness.

cards.ask: Khalid swears "By Allah, I paid you yesterday", knowing that he did not. What does he owe?
options: A sin, with nothing but asking Allah's forgiveness
A kaffara: feeding ten poor people
Nothing at all: it is a slip oath
cards.source: فهذه اليمين يأثم بها صاحبها ولا كفارة فيها إلا الاستغفار
cards.why: He lied on purpose about the past, so this is a ghamus oath. He sins, and only istighfar is left for him, not a kaffara.

cards.title: The binding oath
cards.ar: واليمين المنعقدة: هي الحلف على الأمر المستقبل أن يفعله أو لا يفعله فإذا حنث في ذلك لزمته الكفارة
cards.en: The mun'aqida (binding) oath is swearing about the future: that you will do something, or will not. If you break it (this is called hinth), you must pay the kaffara.

cards.title: The slip oath
cards.ar: واليمين اللغو: أن يحلف على أمر ماض وهو يظن أنه
cards.en: The laghw (slip) oath is swearing about something in the past, truly thinking it is so, when in fact it is not. Al-Quduri says: we hope Allah will not hold the person to account for it.

cards.ask: Amina swears "By Allah, Zayd has arrived", truly believing it. In fact he had not arrived. What kind of oath is this?
options: A laghw oath: we hope Allah does not hold her to account
A ghamus oath: she has sinned
A binding oath: she owes a kaffara
source: واليمين اللغو: أن يحلف على أمر ماض وهو يظن أنه
فهذه نرجو أن لا يؤاخذ الله بها صاحبها
cards.why: She swore about the past and believed it was true, so it is a laghw oath, and al-Quduri hopes she is not held to account.

cards.ask: Which kind of oath is it?
items: "By Allah, I didn't take it", when he knows he did
"By Allah, I will visit you tomorrow"
"By Allah, the shop was open", truly thinking so, but it was shut
"By Allah, I was at home last night", a deliberate lie
source: الحلف على أمر ماض يتعمد الكذب فيه
هي الحلف على الأمر المستقبل أن يفعله أو لا يفعله
أن يحلف على أمر ماض وهو يظن أنه
cards.why: A deliberate lie about the past is ghamus. Any oath about the future is binding. An honest mistake about the past is laghw.

cards.title: Meaning it or not
cards.ar: والقاصد في اليمين والمكره والناسي سواء ومن فعل المحلوف عليه مكرها أو ناسيا سواء
cards.en: An oath counts the same whether the person meant it, was forced (mukrah) to say it, or said it by mistake. And if he does the thing he swore not to do, it counts the same if he was forced or had forgotten.

cards.ask: Umar swore not to drink coffee this week. Then he forgot and drank a cup. Has he broken his oath?
options: No: he forgot, so it doesn't count
Only if he drinks a second cup
cards.source: ومن فعل المحلوف عليه مكرها أو ناسيا سواء
cards.why: Doing the thing you swore against counts the same when forgotten, so he has broken the oath and owes a kaffara.

cards.ask: Which of these are true?

options.text: A ghamus oath has no kaffara, only asking forgiveness
Breaking a binding oath means paying the kaffara
An oath said under force still counts
