A laghw oath is about the future
A ghamus oath is about the future

source: ولا كفارة فيها إلا الاستغفار
فإذا حنث في ذلك لزمته الكفارة
والقاصد في اليمين والمكره والناسي سواء
cards.why: Ghamus has only istighfar, a broken binding oath needs a kaffara, and a forced oath counts. Ghamus and laghw are both about the past.

lessons.title: Words that make an oath
lessons.arabic: واليمين بالله تعالى أو باسم من أسمائه

cards.title: By Allah or His names
cards.ar: واليمين بالله تعالى أو باسم من أسمائه كالرحمن والرحيم
cards.en: An oath is made by swearing by Allah, or by one of His names, such as al-Rahman (the Most Merciful) or al-Rahim (the Most Kind).

cards.title: By His qualities
cards.ar: أو بصفة من صفات ذاته كعزة الله وجلالته وكبريائه إلا قوله: وعلم الله فإنه لا يكون يمينا
cards.en: It is also an oath to swear by a quality of Allah's own being, like His might, majesty or greatness. But saying "By the knowledge of Allah" is not an oath.

cards.ask: Yusuf says: "By the knowledge of Allah, I will not go." Is this an oath?
options: No: al-Quduri makes an exception for "the knowledge of Allah"
Yes: knowledge is a quality of Allah
cards.source: إلا قوله: وعلم الله فإنه لا يكون يمينا
cards.why: Al-Quduri names "By the knowledge of Allah" as the exception: it is not an oath.

cards.title: Qualities of action, and other things
cards.ar: وإن حلف بصفة من صفات الفعل كغضب الله وسخطه لم يكن حالفا
cards.en: Swearing by a quality of Allah's action, like His anger or displeasure, is not an oath. Swearing by anything other than Allah, like the Prophet, the Qur'an or the Kaaba, is not an oath either.

cards.ask: Is it an oath?
source: واليمين بالله تعالى أو باسم من أسمائه
كعزة الله وجلالته وكبريائه
كغضب الله وسخطه لم يكن حالفا
ومن حلف بغير الله لم يكن حالفا كالنبي والقرآن والكعبة
cards.why: Allah, His names and the qualities of His being make an oath. His anger (a quality of action) and things other than Allah do not.

cards.title: Letters of swearing
cards.ar: وحروف القسم: الواو كقوله: والله والباء كقوله: بالله والتاء كقوله: تالله وقد تضمر الحروف فيكون حالفا كقوله: الله لا أفعل كذا
cards.en: In Arabic you swear with a letter: wa (wallahi), bi (billahi) or ta (tallahi). The letter can also be left out, as in "Allahi, I won't do it", and it is still an oath. Abu Hanifa said that "wa haqqi Allah" (by the right of Allah) is not an oath.

cards.ask: The letter can be left out. Complete the example.
cards.ar: وقد تضمر الحروف فيكون حالفا كقوله: ____ لا أفعل كذا
cards.source: وقد تضمر الحروف فيكون حالفا كقوله: الله لا أفعل كذا
cards.why: الله: saying "Allah, I won't do it" with no letter is still an oath.

cards.title: "I swear", "I bear witness"
cards.ar: وإذا قال: أقسم أو أقسم بالله أو أحلف بالله أو أشهد أو أشهد بالله فهو حالف
cards.en: Saying "I swear", "I swear by Allah", "I bear witness" or "I bear witness by Allah" is an oath. So is "By Allah's covenant", "I owe a vow (nadhr)", or "If I do it, I am a Jew, a Christian or a disbeliever".

cards.ask: Hasan says: "I swear (uqsimu) I won't go out today." He did not say "by Allah". Is it an oath?
options: Yes: "I swear" alone is an oath
Only if he also says "I bear witness"
cards.source: وإذا قال: أقسم أو أقسم بالله
cards.why: Al-Quduri lists "I swear" on its own as an oath.

cards.title: Not an oath
cards.ar: وإن قال: علي غضب الله أو سخطه أو أنا زان أو شارب خمر أو آكل ربا فليس بحالف
cards.en: Saying "Allah's anger be on me", or "(if I do it) I am a fornicator, a wine-drinker, or one who eats riba" is not an oath. (Riba is interest: taking extra money on a loan, which Islam forbids.)

cards.ask: Is it an oath?
items: "If I do it, I am a Christian"
"If I do it, Allah's anger be on me"
"If I do it, I am a wine-drinker"
source: وكذلك قوله: وعهد الله وميثاقه وعلي نذر أو نذر الله وإن فعلت كذا فأنا يهودي أو نصراني أو كافر فهو يمين
علي غضب الله أو سخطه أو أنا زان أو شارب خمر أو آكل ربا فليس بحالف
وعلم الله فإنه لا يكون يمينا
cards.why: Allah's covenant, "I am a Christian if..." and "I bear witness by Allah" are oaths. "Allah's anger on me", "I am a wine-drinker" and "by Allah's knowledge" are not.

lessons.title: The kaffara for a broken oath

cards.title: Freeing a slave
cards.ar: وكفارة اليمين: عتق رقبة يجزئ فيها ما يجزئ في
cards.en: The kaffara (making up) for a broken oath has choices. In al-Quduri's time, the first was freeing a slave, and the same slaves count as in the kaffara for zihar (a forbidden way a husband once spoke to his wife).

cards.title: Clothing or feeding ten
cards.ar: وإن شاء كسا عشرة مساكين كل واحد ثوبا فما زاد وأذناه ما تجزئ فيه الصلاة وإن شاء أطعم عشرة مساكين كالإطعام في كفارة الظهار
cards.en: Or, if he likes, he clothes ten poor people, each with a garment or more; the least is clothing you could pray in. Or, if he likes, he feeds ten poor people, the same way as feeding in the zihar kaffara.

cards.ask: How many poor people does he clothe or feed for a broken oath?
cards.source: وإن شاء أطعم عشرة مساكين
cards.why: Al-Quduri says ten poor people, for both clothing and feeding.

cards.title: Fasting three days
cards.ar: فإن لم يقدر على أحد الأشياء الثلاثة صام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات
cards.en: Only if he cannot do any of the three (freeing, clothing, feeding) does he fast, for three days in a row.

cards.ask: Imran broke his oath. He cannot afford to free a slave, clothe or feed ten poor people. What must he do?
options: Fast three days in a row
Fast three days, with gaps allowed
cards.source: صام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات
cards.why: When none of the three is possible, he fasts three days, one after the other.

cards.title: Not before breaking it
cards.ar: فإن قدم الكفارة على الحنث لم يجزه
cards.en: If he pays the kaffara before he breaks the oath, it does not count.

cards.ask: Saad swore not to enter his cousin's house, but he plans to. He feeds ten poor people first and then enters. Is his kaffara done?
options: No: a kaffara before breaking the oath doesn't count
Yes, but he must also fast
cards.source: فإن قدم الكفارة على الحنث لم يجزه
cards.why: He paid before he broke the oath, so it does not count. He owes the kaffara after breaking it.

cards.title: An oath to do wrong
cards.ar: ومن حلف على معصية مثل أن لا يصلي أو لا يكلم أباه أو ليقتلن فلانا فينبغي أن يحنث ويكفر عن يمينه
cards.en: If someone swears to do a sin, like not praying, not speaking to his father, or killing someone, he should break the oath and pay the kaffara.

cards.ask: Tariq angrily swore never to speak to his father again. What should he do?
options: Break the oath, speak to his father, and pay the kaffara
Keep the oath, because an oath is an oath
cards.source: فينبغي أن يحنث ويكفر عن يمينه
cards.why: Not speaking to his father is a sin, so he should break the oath and pay its kaffara.

cards.title: A non-Muslim's oath
cards.ar: وإذا حلف الكافر ثم حنث في حال الكفر أو بعد إسلامه فلا حنث عليه
cards.en: If a non-Muslim swears and then breaks it, whether before or after becoming Muslim, it does not count as breaking an oath.

cards.ask: Which of these are true?

options.text: The kaffara can be clothing ten poor people
Fasting is only for someone who cannot do the other three
A kaffara paid before breaking the oath doesn't count
The fast is ten days
A non-Muslim who swore and broke it after Islam owes a kaffara

source: وإن شاء كسا عشرة مساكين
فإن لم يقدر على أحد الأشياء الثلاثة صام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات
فإن قدم الكفارة على الحنث لم يجزه
فلا حنث عليه
cards.why: Clothing ten is one choice, fasting comes only when the others are impossible, and early kaffara doesn't count. The fast is three days, and a non-Muslim's oath has no breaking.

lessons.title: Making things haram on yourself, and vows
lessons.arabic: ومن نذر نذرا مطلقا فعليه الوفاء به

cards.title: Calling your own thing haram
cards.ar: ومن حرم على نفسه شيئا مما يملكه لم يصر محرما لعينه
cards.en: If someone declares something he owns haram (forbidden) for himself, it does not really become haram. But if he then uses it, he owes the kaffara of an oath.

cards.ask: Layla says "This cake is haram for me", then eats it. What happens?
options: She owes the kaffara of an oath
She has sinned and must only ask forgiveness
source: لم يصر محرما لعينه
استباحه كفارة يمين
cards.why: The cake did not become haram, but by eating it after her words she owes an oath's kaffara.

cards.title: "Everything halal is haram for me"
cards.ar: فإن قال: كل حلال علي حرام فهو على الطعام والشراب إلا أن ينوي غير ذلك
cards.en: If he says "Everything halal is haram for me", it is taken to mean food and drink, unless he meant something else.

cards.ask: Rashid says "Everything halal is haram for me", without meaning anything in particular. What does it cover?
cards.source: فهو على الطعام والشراب إلا أن ينوي غير ذلك
cards.why: With no particular intention, it is understood to be about food and drink.

cards.title: Keeping a vow
cards.ar: ومن نذر نذرا مطلقا فعليه الوفاء به
cards.en: A nadhr is a vow: promising Allah to do a good deed. If someone makes a plain vow with no condition, he must fulfil it.

cards.title: A vow with a condition
cards.ar: وإن علق نذره بشرط فوجد الشرط فعليه الوفاء بنفس النذر
cards.en: If he ties his vow to a condition ("If this happens, I will...") and the condition happens, he must fulfil the vow itself.

cards.title: Abu Hanifa's later view
cards.ar: وروي أن أبا حنيفة رجع عن ذلك وقال: إذا قال: إن فعلت كذا فعلي حجة أو صوم سنة أو صدقة ما أملكه أجزأه من ذلك كفارة يمين وهو قول محمد
cards.en: Note: it is reported that Abu Hanifa later changed his view. If someone says "If I do such-and-such, I owe a Hajj, a year of fasting, or giving away all I own", an oath's kaffara is enough for him. This is also Muhammad's view.

cards.ask: Huda vows: "I will fast three days for Allah", with no condition. What must she do?
options: Nothing, unless she adds a condition
cards.source: ومن نذر نذرا مطلقا فعليه الوفاء به
cards.why: A plain vow must be fulfilled.

cards.ask: What does he owe?
items: Says "My car is haram for me", then drives it
Says "This bread is haram for me", then eats it
Vows a day's fast, with no condition
Vows "If I recover, I'll give 10 dirhams in charity", and recovers
source: وعليه أن استباحه كفارة يمين
ومن نذر نذرا مطلقا فعليه الوفاء به
فوجد الشرط فعليه الوفاء بنفس النذر
cards.why: Using something you called haram costs an oath's kaffara. A plain vow, or a conditional vow whose condition happens, must be fulfilled.

cards.title: "I won't enter a house"
cards.ar: لا يدخل بيتا فدخل الكعبة أو المسجد أو البيعة أو الكنيسة لم يحنث
cards.en: Oaths are understood by how people normally speak. A bayt is a house to live in. So if someone swears not to enter a bayt and then enters the Kaaba, a mosque, a synagogue or a church, he has not broken his oath.

cards.ask: Musa swore "By Allah, I won't enter a house today". Then he went into the mosque to pray. Has he broken his oath?
options: No: a mosque is not a house
Yes: he went into a building
Yes, unless he stayed outside the prayer hall
cards.source: لا يدخل بيتا فدخل الكعبة أو المسجد
cards.why: Entering a mosque does not break an oath about entering a house.

cards.title: Reciting in prayer
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يتكلم فقرأ في الصلاة لم يحنث
cards.en: If someone swears not to speak, and then recites Qur'an in his prayer, he has not broken the oath.

cards.ask: Ziyad swore not to say a word all afternoon. He then prayed Asr and recited the Fatiha. What is the ruling?
options: Not broken: reciting in prayer is not speaking
cards.source: ومن حلف لا يتكلم فقرأ في الصلاة لم يحنث
cards.why: Al-Quduri says reciting in the prayer does not break an oath not to speak.

cards.title: Taking it off at once
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يلبس ثوبا وهو لابسه فنزعه في الحال لم يحنث وكذا إذا حلف لا يركب هذه الدابة وهو راكبها فنزل في الحال وإن لبث ساعة حنث
cards.en: If someone wearing a garment swears not to wear it, and takes it off at once, he has not broken the oath. The same goes for swearing not to ride an animal while on it, and getting off at once. If he stays on for a while, he has broken it.

cards.ask: Bilal, riding his camel, swears not to ride this camel. He stays on it for an hour. What is the ruling?
options: Broken: he stayed on for a while
Not broken: he was already riding
Not broken, as long as he gets off later
cards.source: وإن لبث ساعة حنث
cards.why: He did not get off at once, so staying on counts as riding.

cards.title: Already inside
cards.ar: وإن حلف لا يدخل هذه الدار وهو فيها لم يحنث بالقعود حتى يخرج ثم يدخل
cards.en: If someone inside a house (dar) swears not to enter it, sitting there does not break it. Only going out and coming back in does.

cards.title: A ruined house
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يدخل دارا فدخل دارا خرابا لم يحنث
cards.en: If he swears not to enter "a house" (dar, any house) and enters a ruined one, he has not broken it.

cards.title: "This house" after it falls
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يدخل هذه الدار فدخلها بعد ما انهدمت وصارت صحراء حنث ولو حلف لا يدخل هذا البيت فدخله بعد ما انهدم لم يحنث
cards.en: But if he swore not to enter "this dar" (a particular house with its yard), then entered it after it fell down into open ground, he has broken it. If he swore not to enter "this bayt" (this roofed room) and entered after it collapsed, he has not.

cards.ask: Broken or not?
items: Swore not to enter "this dar"; entered after it became open ground
Swore not to ride this horse while on it; stayed on an hour
Swore not to enter "a dar"; entered a ruined one
Swore not to enter "this bayt"; entered after it collapsed
Wearing a coat, swore not to wear it; took it off at once
Inside a house, swore not to enter it; sat there
source: فدخلها بعد ما انهدمت وصارت صحراء حنث
وإن لبث ساعة حنث
فدخل دارا خرابا لم يحنث
فدخله بعد ما انهدم لم يحنث
فنزعه في الحال لم يحنث
لم يحنث بالقعود حتى يخرج ثم يدخل
cards.why: "This dar" stays itself even as open ground, and staying on counts as riding. A ruin is not "a dar", a fallen bayt is no bayt, and taking off at once or sitting inside is not wearing or entering.

lessons.title: When people and things change
lessons.arabic: ومن حلف لا يكلم زوجة فلان

cards.title: Someone's wife
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يكلم زوجة فلان فطلقها فلان ثم كلمها حنث
cards.en: If someone swears not to speak to a certain man's wife, and the man then divorces her, speaking to her afterwards still breaks the oath.

cards.ask: Faris swore not to speak to Hamid's wife. Hamid later divorced her, and Faris spoke to her. What is the ruling?
options: Not broken: she is no longer Hamid's wife
Broken only if he knew of the divorce
cards.source: فطلقها فلان ثم كلمها حنث
cards.why: Al-Quduri says he has broken the oath, even after the divorce.

cards.title: Someone's slave or house, once sold
cards.ar: ولو حلف لا يكلم عبد فلان أو لا يدخل دار فلان فباع عبده وداره ثم كلم العبد ودخل الدار لم يحنث
cards.en: If he swears not to speak to a man's slave (in al-Quduri's time) or not to enter a man's house, and the man sells them, speaking to that slave or entering that house afterwards does not break it.

cards.ask: Nabil swore not to enter Hamza's house. Hamza sold the house, and Nabil then went in. What is the ruling?
options: Not broken: it is no longer Hamza's house
Broken: it is the same building
Broken if Nabil pointed at it
cards.source: أو لا يدخل دار فلان فباع عبده وداره ثم كلم العبد ودخل الدار لم يحنث
cards.why: After the sale, the house no longer belongs to Hamza, so entering it does not break the oath.

cards.title: The same person, the same thing
cards.ar: وإن حلف لا يكلم صاحب هذا الطيلسان فباعه ثم كلمه حنث وكذلك إن حلف لا يكلم هذا الشاب فكلمه بعد ما صار شيخا حنث أو لا يأكل لحم هذا الحمل فصار كبشا فأكله حنث
cards.en: If he swears not to speak to "the owner of this taylasan" (a scarf worn over the shoulders), and the owner sells it, speaking to him still breaks it. So does speaking to "this young man" after he grows old, or eating "this lamb" after it grows into a ram.

cards.ask: Idris swore not to speak to "the owner of this shawl". The owner sold the shawl, and Idris spoke to him. What is the ruling?
options: Broken: he is still the same man
Not broken: he no longer owns the shawl
Not broken, unless Idris knew the man
cards.source: وإن حلف لا يكلم صاحب هذا الطيلسان فباعه ثم كلمه حنث
cards.why: Al-Quduri rules that he has broken the oath: selling the shawl does not change who the man is.

cards.title: Palm trees and dates
cards.ar: وإن حلف لا يأكل من هذه النخلة فهو على ثمرها وإن حلف لا يأكل من هذا البسر فصار رطبا فأكله لم يحنث وإن حلف لا يأكل بسرا فأكل رطبا لم يحنث
cards.en: Swearing not to eat from "this palm tree" means its fruit. Busr are unripe dates and rutab are ripe, fresh dates. If he swears not to eat "this busr" and eats it after it ripens into rutab, or swears not to eat busr and eats rutab, he has not broken the oath.

cards.title: Dates starting to ripen
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يأكل رطبا فأكل بسرا مذنبا حنث عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: If he swears not to eat rutab, and eats busr that has started ripening at the tip, Abu Hanifa says he has broken it.

cards.title: Meat and fish
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يأكل لحما فأكل السمك لم يحنث
cards.en: If he swears not to eat meat (lahm) and eats fish, he has not broken it.

cards.title: Drinking from the Tigris
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يشرب من دجله فشرب منها بإناء لم يحنث حتى يكرع منها كرعا في قول أبي حنيفة ومن حلف لا يشرب من ماء دجلة فشرب منها بإناء حنث
cards.en: The Tigris (Dijla) is a great river in Iraq. If he swears not to drink "from the Tigris" and drinks with a cup, Abu Hanifa says he has not broken it until he drinks straight from the river with his mouth. If he swears not to drink "from the water of the Tigris", drinking it from a cup does break it.

cards.ask: Broken or not?
items: Swore not to speak to "this young man"; spoke to him when old
Swore not to eat "this lamb"; ate it once it was a ram
Swore not to drink "the water of the Tigris"; drank it from a cup
Swore not to eat "this busr"; ate it once it was rutab
Swore not to eat meat; ate fish
Swore not to enter Ali's house; entered after Ali sold it
source: فكلمه بعد ما صار شيخا حنث
فصار كبشا فأكله حنث
ومن حلف لا يشرب من ماء دجلة فشرب منها بإناء حنث
فصار رطبا فأكله لم يحنث
فأكل السمك لم يحنث
فباع عبده وداره ثم كلم العبد ودخل الدار لم يحنث
cards.why: A person or animal pointed at stays the same as it grows, and the water of the Tigris is the same in a cup. Busr that became rutab, fish, and a house that was sold are different.

lessons.title: Wheat, flour, speaking and the doorway
lessons.arabic: ومن حلف لا يأكل من هذه الحنطة

cards.title: Wheat and its bread
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يأكل من هذه الحنطة فأكل من خبزها لم يحنث
cards.en: If someone swears not to eat "from this wheat" and eats bread made from it, he has not broken the oath.

cards.title: Flour and its bread
cards.ar: من خبزه حنث ولو استفه كما هو لم يحنث
cards.en: But if he swears not to eat "from this flour" and eats bread made from it, he has broken it. If he swallows the dry flour as it is, he has not, since people don't usually eat flour that way.

cards.ask: Sami swore not to eat from this sack of wheat. His mother ground it and baked bread, and he ate it. What is the ruling?
options: Broken only if he ate the whole loaf
cards.source: ومن حلف لا يأكل من هذه الحنطة فأكل من خبزها لم يحنث
cards.why: For wheat, eating its bread does not break the oath. (For flour, it would.)

cards.title: Speaking to someone asleep
cards.ar: ولو حلف لا يكلم فلانا فكلمه وهو بحيث يسمع إلا أنه نائم حنث
cards.en: If he swears not to speak to someone, then speaks to him close enough to be heard, but the person is asleep, he has broken it.

cards.title: Permission he didn't know of
cards.ar: وإن حلف لا يكلمه إلا بإذنه فأذن له ولم يعلم بالأذن حتى كلمه حنث
cards.en: If he swears not to speak to someone without that person's permission, and permission is given but he does not know about it before speaking, he has broken it.

cards.ask: Jamal swore not to speak to Tariq without Tariq's permission. Tariq told someone "He may speak to me", but Jamal never heard this. Jamal spoke to him. What is the ruling?
options: Broken: he didn't know of the permission
Not broken, if Tariq didn't mind
cards.source: فأذن له ولم يعلم بالأذن حتى كلمه حنث
cards.why: Permission he did not know about doesn't help him, so he has broken the oath.

cards.title: The governor's oath
cards.ar: وإذا استحلف الوالي رجلا ليعلمه بكل داعر دخل البلد فهذا على حال ولايته خاصة
cards.en: If a governor makes a man swear to tell him of every da'ir (troublemaker) who comes to town, the oath lasts only while that governor is in office.

cards.ask: The governor made Hisham swear to report every troublemaker who enters the city. The governor was later removed. Must Hisham still report to him?
options: No: the oath was only for his time in office
Yes, to whoever is the new governor
cards.source: فهذا على حال ولايته خاصة
cards.why: The oath is tied to his governorship and ends with it.

cards.title: The slave's animal
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يركب دابة فلان فركب دابة عبده لم يحنث
cards.en: If he swears not to ride a certain man's animal and rides the animal of that man's slave (in al-Quduri's time), he has not broken it.

cards.title: Roof and hallway
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يدخل هذه الدار فوقف على سطحها أو دخل دهليزها حنث
cards.en: If he swears not to enter this house, and stands on its roof or enters its entrance hall, he has broken it.

cards.ask: Ayyub swore not to enter this house. He stood inside the arch of the doorway, so that if the door were shut he would be outside. What is the ruling?
options: Broken: he was in the doorway
Broken, like standing on the roof
source: وإن وقف في طاق الباب
إذا أغلق الباب كان خارجا لم يحنث
cards.why: If shutting the door would leave him outside, he has not entered, so he has not broken it.

cards.ask: Broken or not?
items: Swore not to eat this flour; ate bread made from it
Swore not to enter this house; stood on its roof
Swore not to speak to Ali; spoke to him while he slept nearby
Swore not to eat this wheat; ate bread made from it
Swore not to eat this flour; swallowed it dry
Swore not to ride Ali's animal; rode his slave's animal
source: من خبزه حنث ولو استفه كما هو لم يحنث
فوقف على سطحها أو دخل دهليزها حنث
إلا أنه نائم حنث
فأكل من خبزها لم يحنث
فركب دابة عبده لم يحنث
cards.why: Flour's bread, the roof, and speaking within hearing all break it. Wheat's bread, dry flour, and the slave's animal do not.

lessons.title: What words mean: food, agents, sitting

cards.title: Roast
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يأكل الشواء فهو على اللحم دون الباذنجان والجزر
cards.en: Words in an oath mean what people usually mean by them. "Roast" means roasted meat, not roasted aubergine or carrots.

cards.title: Cooked food
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يأكل الطبيخ فهو على ما يطبخ من اللحم
cards.en: "Cooked food" (tabikh) means meat that is cooked.

cards.ask: Yasir swore not to eat roast. At a barbecue he ate grilled aubergine. What is the ruling?
options: Broken only if he ate a lot
cards.source: فهو على اللحم دون الباذنجان والجزر
cards.why: "Roast" is about meat only, so aubergine does not break it.

cards.title: Heads
cards.ar: على ما يكبس في التنانير ويباع في المصر
cards.en: If he swears not to eat "heads", it means the heads that are baked in ovens and sold in town (like sheep's heads), not every head.

cards.title: Bread
cards.ar: على ما يعتاد أهل البلد أكله خبزا فإن أكل خبز القطائف أو خبز الأرز بالعراق لم يحنث
cards.en: "Bread" means what the people of that town normally eat as bread. So eating qata'if (a sweet pancake) or rice bread in Iraq does not break it.

cards.ask: In Iraq, Rami swore not to eat bread. He ate some rice bread. What is the ruling?
options: Not broken: rice bread is not the usual bread there
cards.source: فإن أكل خبز القطائف أو خبز الأرز بالعراق لم يحنث
cards.why: Bread means the town's usual bread, and al-Quduri names rice bread in Iraq as not counting.

cards.title: Using an agent to sell
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يبيع أو لا يشتري أولا يؤاجر فوكل بذلك لم يحنث
cards.en: If he swears not to sell, buy or rent out, and then appoints a wakil (an agent who acts for him) to do it, he has not broken the oath.

cards.title: Using an agent to marry
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يتزوج أو لا يطلق
cards.en: But if he swears not to marry, or not to divorce, or not to free a slave, and then appoints an agent to do it, he has broken it.

cards.ask: He swore not to do it, then had an agent do it. Broken or not?
items: An agent sells his car for him
An agent buys a phone for him
An agent rents out his flat for him
source: ومن حلف لا يبيع أو لا يشتري أولا يؤاجر فوكل بذلك لم يحنث
ومن حلف لا يتزوج أو لا يطلق
cards.why: For marrying and divorcing, an agent's act counts as his own. For selling, buying and renting, it does not.

cards.title: Sitting on the ground
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يجلس على الأرض فجلس على بساط أو حصير لم يحنث
cards.en: If he swears not to sit on the ground, and sits on a carpet or a mat, he has not broken it.

cards.ask: Hadi swore not to sit on a bed. He sat on a bed with a blanket spread on it. What is the ruling?
options: Broken: it is still the bed
Not broken: he sat on the blanket
Not broken, unless the bed was his
cards.source: ومن حلف لا يجلس على سرير فجلس على سرير فوقه بساط حنث وإن جعل فوقه سريرا فجلس عليه لم يحنث
cards.why: A blanket on a bed is still sitting on the bed. Only another bed on top would change it.

cards.ask: Which of these break the oath?

options.text: Swore not to sleep on a mattress; slept on it with a sheet on top
Swore not to divorce; had an agent divorce for him
Swore not to eat roast; ate roast lamb
Swore not to sleep on a mattress; slept on another mattress laid on top
Swore not to sit on the ground; sat on a mat

source: وإن حلف لا ينام على فراش فنام عليه
وإن جعل فوقه فراشا آخر لم يحنث
ومن حلف لا يتزوج أو لا يطلق
فهو على اللحم
فجلس على بساط أو حصير لم يحنث
cards.why: A sheet doesn't change the mattress, divorce by an agent counts, and roast lamb is roast. A second mattress on top, or a mat on the ground, makes it something else.

lessons.title: In sha Allah, time words, permission
lessons.arabic: ومن حلف بيمين وقال: إن شاء الله

cards.title: Saying in sha Allah
cards.ar: ومن حلف بيمين وقال: إن شاء الله متصلا بيمينه فلا حنث عليه
cards.en: If someone swears and says "in sha Allah" (if Allah wills) straight after the oath, joined to it, he cannot break it.

cards.ask: Karim says "By Allah, I'll beat you in the race, in sha Allah" in one breath. He loses. What is the ruling?
options: No breaking: he joined in sha Allah to the oath
cards.source: متصلا بيمينه فلا حنث عليه
cards.why: In sha Allah joined to the oath means there is no breaking it.

cards.title: "If I am able"
cards.ar: وإن حلف ليأتينه إن استطاع فهذا على استطاعة الصحة دون القدرة
cards.en: If he swears "I will come to him, if I am able", it means being healthy and free of obstacles, not merely having the power to do it.

cards.title: "A while"
cards.ar: وإن حلف لا يكلم فلانا حينا أو زمانا أو الحين أو الزمان فهو على ستة أشهر
cards.en: If he swears not to speak to someone for "a while" (hin or zaman), it means six months. Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say the same for "an age" (dahr).

cards.ask: Omar swore not to speak to his cousin "for a while". How long does the oath last?
cards.source: حينا أو زمانا أو الحين أو الزمان فهو على ستة أشهر
cards.why: Al-Quduri says "a while" means six months.

cards.title: "Days"
cards.ar: ولو حلف لا يكلمه أياما على ثلاثة أيام
cards.en: If he swears not to speak to him for "days" (ayyaman), it means three days. For "the days" (al-ayyam), Abu Hanifa says ten days; Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say the days of the week. For "the months", Abu Hanifa says ten months; they say twelve.

cards.ask: Nadia swore not to speak to her friend for "days" (ayyaman). How long is that?
cards.source: ولو حلف لا يكلمه أياما على ثلاثة أيام
cards.why: "Days" without "the" means three days.

cards.title: Not doing, and doing
cards.ar: وإذا حلف لا يفعل كذا تركه أبدا وإن حلف ليفعلن كذا ففعله مرة واحدة بر في يمينه
cards.en: If he swears not to do something, he must leave it for ever. If he swears he will do something, doing it once keeps the oath.

cards.ask: Salim swore "I will visit my grandmother". He visited her once. Has he kept his oath?
options: Only if he stays a whole day
cards.source: وإن حلف ليفعلن كذا ففعله مرة واحدة بر في يمينه
cards.why: An oath to do something is kept by doing it once.

cards.title: "Except with my permission"
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا تخرج امرأته إلا بإذنه فأذن لها مرة فخرجت ثم خرجت مرة أخرى بغير إذنه حنث ولا بد من إذن في كل خروج
cards.en: If a man swears his wife will not go out "except with his permission", every outing needs permission. If she goes once with permission and later without it, he has broken the oath.

cards.ask: Broken or not?
items: "Except with my permission": went once with it, then once without
"Not for a while": spoke after two months
"Until I permit you": went once with permission, then without
Swore and joined in sha Allah to it
"Not for days": spoke after four days
source: ولا بد من إذن في كل خروج
فهو على ستة أشهر
وإن قال: إلا أن آذن لك فأذن لها مرة ثم خرجت بعدها بغير إذنه لم يحنث
متصلا بيمينه فلا حنث عليه
على ثلاثة أيام
cards.why: "Except with my permission" needs it every time, and "a while" is six months. "Until I permit you" ends with the first permission, in sha Allah stops the breaking, and "days" ends after three.

cards.title: Meal times
cards.ar: وإذا حلف لا يتغدى فالغداء الأكل من طلوع الفجر إلى الظهر والعشاء من صلاة الظهر إلى نصف الليل والسحور من نصف الليل إلى طلوع الفجر
cards.en: Ghada' (the day meal) is eating from dawn to midday (Dhuhr). 'Asha' (the evening meal) is from the Dhuhr prayer to midnight. Suhur is from midnight to dawn.

cards.ask: Fahad swore not to eat ghada' today. He ate at 11 in the morning. What is the ruling?
options: Not broken: ghada' is after Dhuhr
cards.source: فالغداء الأكل من طلوع الفجر إلى الظهر
cards.why: Ghada' runs from dawn to Dhuhr, so 11am is ghada'.

cards.title: "Soon" and "later"
cards.ar: وإن حلف ليقضين دينه إلى قريب فهو ما دون الشهر وإن قال: إلى بعيد فهو أكثر من الشهر
cards.en: If he swears to pay his debt "soon", it means under a month. "Later" (a long time) means more than a month.

cards.ask: Mahmud swore to repay his debt "soon". By when must he pay?
cards.source: إلى قريب فهو ما دون الشهر
cards.why: "Soon" means less than a month.

cards.title: Moving out
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يسكن هذه الدار فخرج منها نفسه وترك فيها أهله ومتاعه حنث
cards.en: If he swears not to live in this house, then leaves himself but leaves his family and belongings in it, he has broken the oath.

cards.title: Swearing the impossible
cards.ar: ومن حلف ليصعد السماء
cards.en: If he swears to climb into the sky, or to turn a stone into gold, the oath is made, and it is broken straight away.

cards.ask: In anger, Badr swore "By Allah, I will turn this stone into gold!" What is the ruling?
options: The oath is made and broken at once, so he owes a kaffara
It is not an oath, since it is impossible
cards.source: انعقدت يمينه وحنث عقيبها
cards.why: Al-Quduri says the oath is made and broken straight after it.

cards.title: Paying with bad coins
cards.ar: ومن حلف ليقضين فلانا دينه اليوم فقضاه ثم وجد فلان بعضه زيوفا أو نبهرجة أو مستحقة لم يحنث وإن وجدها رصاصا أو ستوقة حنث
cards.en: If he swears to pay a debt today and pays, then some coins turn out to be zuyuf or nabahraja (poor silver coins that merchants refuse), or belong to someone else, he has not broken the oath. If they turn out to be lead, or sattuqa (copper with a thin silver coat), he has broken it.

cards.ask: Hakim swore to pay Zubair today, and paid. Later Zubair found some of the coins were lead. What is the ruling?
options: Broken: lead coins are not payment
Not broken, if he replaces them
cards.source: وإن وجدها رصاصا أو ستوقة حنث
cards.why: Lead is not money at all, so the debt was not really paid that day.

cards.title: Collecting in parts
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يقبض دينه درهما دون درهم فقبض بعضه لم يحنث حتى يقبض متفرقا وإن قبض دينه في وزنتين لم يتشاغل بينهما إلا بعمل الوزن لم يحنث
cards.en: If he swears not to collect his debt bit by bit, collecting some of it does not break the oath until he collects all of it in separate parts. Collecting it in two weighings, busy only with weighing in between, does not break it: that is not splitting it up.

cards.title: "I will go to Basra"
cards.ar: ومن حلف ليأتين البصرة فلم يأتها حتى مات حنث في آخر جزء من أجزاء حياته
cards.en: If he swears "I will go to Basra" and never goes before he dies, he breaks it in the last moment of his life.

cards.ask: Which of these break the oath?

options.text: Swore not to live here; left, but left his family and things
Swore to go to Basra; died without going
Swore to pay today; the coins were sattuqa
Swore to pay today; some coins were zuyuf
Swore not to collect bit by bit; collected in two weighings back to back

source: وترك فيها أهله ومتاعه حنث
حنث في آخر جزء من أجزاء حياته
وإن وجدها رصاصا أو ستوقة حنث
زيوفا أو نبهرجة أو مستحقة لم يحنث
وليس ذلك بتفريق
cards.why: Leaving family and things behind, dying before Basra, and sattuqa coins all break it. Zuyuf coins and two weighings back to back do not.

lessons.title: Claimant, defendant and the judge
lessons.arabic: المدعي: من لا يجبر على الخصومة إذا تركها

cards.title: Who is who
cards.ar: المدعي: من لا يجبر على الخصومة إذا تركها والمدعى عليه: من يجبر على الخصومة
cards.en: A da'wa is a claim brought before a judge. The mudda'i (claimant) is the one who would not be forced to carry on the case if he dropped it. The mudda'a 'alayh (defendant) is the one who is forced to answer it.

cards.ask: Ahmad says Bilal owes him 100 dirhams. Bilal says he owes nothing. Who is the claimant?
options: Ahmad: nobody forces him to keep the case going
cards.source: المدعي: من لا يجبر على الخصومة إذا تركها
cards.why: Ahmad could drop the case and no one would force him on, so he is the claimant.

cards.title: A clear claim
cards.ar: ولا تقبل الدعوى حتى يذكر شيئا معلوما في جنسه وقدره
cards.en: A claim is only heard if it names something known, by its kind and its amount. If it is an object held by the defendant, he must bring it so it can be pointed at; if it is not there, its value is given. Land must be described by its boundaries and said to be held by the defendant. A debt owed must be said to be demanded.

cards.ask: What must a claim include?

options.text: The kind of thing claimed
Its amount
For land: its boundaries, and that the defendant holds it
For a missing object: its value
The claimant's age
Four witnesses

source: حتى يذكر شيئا معلوما في جنسه وقدره
وإن ادعى عقارا حدده وذكر أنه في يد المدعى عليه
وإن لم تكن حاضرة ذكر قيمتها
cards.why: Al-Quduri asks for the kind, the amount, the boundaries of land and who holds it, and the value of an absent object. Age and a number of witnesses are not part of the claim.

cards.title: What the judge does
cards.ar: فإذا صحت الدعوى سأل القاضي المدعى عليه عنها فإن اعترف قضى عليه بها وإن أنكر سأل المدعى البينة فإن أحضرها قضى بها وإن عجز عن ذلك وطلب يمين خصمه استحلف عليها
cards.en: When the claim is valid, the judge asks the defendant. If he admits it, the judge rules against him. If he denies it, the judge asks the claimant for bayyina (proof by witnesses). If he brings it, the judge rules by it. If he cannot, and asks for the defendant's oath, the defendant is made to swear.

cards.ask: Put the steps of a case in order.
steps: The claim is checked as valid
The judge asks the claimant for proof
The claimant has none and asks for the defendant's oath
The defendant is made to swear
source: فإذا صحت الدعوى سأل القاضي المدعى عليه عنها
وإن أنكر سأل المدعى البينة
وإن عجز عن ذلك وطلب يمين خصمه استحلف عليها
cards.why: Valid claim, question, denial, proof asked for, and only when there is none, the defendant's oath.

cards.title: The oath is not turned back
cards.ar: فإن قال: لي بينة وطلب اليمين لم يستحلف عند أبي حنيفة ولا ترد اليمين على المدعي
cards.en: The oath is never turned back onto the claimant: he does not win by swearing himself. Abu Hanifa also said: if the claimant says "I have proof here" but asks for the oath, the defendant is not made to swear.

cards.title: The holder's proof
cards.ar: ولا تقبل بينه صاحب اليد في الملك المطلق
cards.en: The "one with the hand" (sahib al-yad) is the person holding the thing. When the claim is plain ownership, with no reason given, the holder's proof is not accepted; the claimant's is.

cards.title: Refusing to swear
cards.ar: وإذا نكل المدعى عليه عن اليمين قضي عليه بالنكول ولزمه ما ادعى عليه
cards.en: Nukul means refusing to swear. If the defendant refuses, the judge rules against him for refusing, and he owes what was claimed.

cards.title: Three offers
cards.ar: وينبغي للقاضي أن يقول له: إني أعرض اليمين عليك ثلاثا فإن حلفت وإلا قضيت عليك بما ادعاه فإذا كرر العرض ثلاث مرات قضى عليه بالنكول
cards.en: The judge should tell him: "I will offer you the oath three times. Swear, or I will rule against you." After offering three times, he rules against him for refusing.

cards.ask: Bilal refuses to swear. How many times should the judge offer him the oath before ruling against him?
cards.source: فإذا كرر العرض ثلاث مرات قضى عليه بالنكول
cards.why: The judge offers the oath three times, then rules.

cards.ask: Bilal refuses to swear. Ahmad says: "Then let me swear instead." What happens?
options: Ahmad may not swear; Bilal's refusal decides it against him
source: ولا ترد اليمين على المدعي
قضي عليه بالنكول ولزمه ما ادعى عليه
cards.why: The oath is not turned back onto the claimant. Bilal's refusal itself makes him owe the 100 dirhams.

lessons.title: No oath in some claims; two claimants

cards.title: Where no oath is taken
cards.ar: وإن كانت الدعوى نكاحا لم يستحلف المنكر عند أبي حنيفة ولا يستحلف في النكاح والرجعة والفيء في الإيلاء والرق والاستيلاد والنسب والولاء والحدود
cards.en: In some claims, Abu Hanifa says the one who denies is not made to swear: marriage; raj'a (a husband taking his wife back after a divorce); fay' in an ila (returning to a wife after swearing to keep away from her); being a slave (in al-Quduri's time); istilad (a slave woman bearing her master's child); nasab (lineage); wala' (a tie with a freed slave); and hudud (fixed punishments).

cards.title: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad
cards.ar: وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: يستحلف في ذلك كله إلا في الحدود والقصاص
cards.en: Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say an oath is taken in all of these, except hudud and qisas (equal retaliation for an injury).

cards.ask: In which claims does al-Quduri's list say the denier is NOT made to swear?

options.text: A claim of marriage
A claim about lineage (nasab)
A claim of a hadd punishment
A claim of a 100-dirham debt
A claim to a house

cards.source: ولا يستحلف في النكاح والرجعة والفيء في الإيلاء والرق والاستيلاد والنسب والولاء والحدود
cards.why: Marriage, lineage and hudud are on al-Quduri's list. Debts and property are not, so the oath is taken there.

cards.title: Two claimants with proof
cards.ar: وإذا ادعى اثنان عينا في يد آخر كل واحد منهما يزعم أنها له وأقاما البينة قضي بها بينهما
cards.en: If two people claim an object held by a third, each saying it is his, and both bring proof, it is given to them both, shared.

cards.ask: Ali and Umar each claim a horse that Zayd is holding, and both bring proof. Who gets it?
cards.source: قضي بها بينهما
cards.why: Both proved it, so it is ruled between them.

cards.title: Two men, one woman
cards.ar: وإن ادعى كل واحد منهما نكاح امرأة وأقاما البينة لم يقض بواحدة من البينتين ويرجع إلى تصديق المرأة لأحدهما
cards.en: If two men each claim to have married the same woman and both bring proof, neither proof is ruled on. The matter goes back to which of them the woman confirms.

cards.ask: Two men each bring witnesses that they married Hind. What decides it?
options: Which man Hind says is her husband
Neither: she is married to both
cards.source: ويرجع إلى تصديق المرأة لأحدهما
cards.why: Neither proof is used; it goes back to her confirming one of them.

cards.title: Two buyers
cards.ar: وإن ادعى اثنان كل واحد منهما أنه اشترى منه هذا العبد وأقاما البينة فكل واحد منهما بالخيار: إن شاء أخذ نصف العبد بنصف الثمن وإن شاء ترك
cards.en: If two people each prove they bought the same item from the holder (al-Quduri's example is a slave, in his time), each may choose: take half for half the price, or leave it.

cards.title: Dates and possession
cards.ar: فإن قضى القاضي بينهما به فقال أحدهما: لا أختار لم يكن للآخر أن يأخذ جميعه وإن ذكر واحد منهما تاريخا فهو للأول منهما وإن لم يذكرا ومع أحدهما قبض فهو أولى به
cards.en: If the judge has split it and one says "I don't want it", the other cannot then take all of it. If a date is given, it goes to the earlier buyer. With no dates, the one who has qabd (taken possession) has the better claim.

cards.ask: Two men each prove they bought the same car from Zayd. Neither gives a date, but one already has the car. Who has the better claim?
options: The one who has the car
They split it half each, no choice
cards.source: وإن لم يذكرا ومع أحدهما قبض فهو أولى به
cards.why: With no dates, the one who has taken possession comes first.

cards.ask: Which word completes it?
cards.ar: ويرجع إلى تصديق ____ لأحدهما
cards.source: ويرجع إلى تصديق المرأة لأحدهما
cards.why: المرأة: when two men prove a marriage to her, it goes back to which one she confirms.

cards.title: Purchase or gift
cards.ar: وإن ادعى أحدهما شراء والآخر هبة وقبضا وأقاما البينة ولا تاريخ معهما فالشراء أولى
cards.en: If one claims he bought it and the other says it was a hiba (gift) to him, each having taken it, and both bring proof with no dates, the purchase wins.

cards.title: Purchase or mahr
cards.ar: وإن ادعى أحدهما الشراء وادعت امرأة أنه تزوجها عليه فهما سواء
cards.en: If one claims he bought it, and a woman claims it was given as her mahr (the gift a husband gives his bride), they are equal.

cards.title: Pledge or gift
cards.ar: وإن ادعى أحدهما رهنا وقبضا والآخر هبة وقبضا فالرهن أولى
cards.en: If one claims it was pledged to him as rahn (security for a debt) and the other says it was a gift, each having taken it, the pledge wins.

cards.ask: Hamza proves he bought a watch from Malik; Sami proves Malik gave it to him as a gift. Both took it, and no dates are given. Whose claim wins?
cards.source: ولا تاريخ معهما فالشراء أولى
cards.why: With no dates, purchase beats gift.

cards.title: Earlier dates
cards.ar: وإن أقام الخارجان البينة على الملك والتاريخ فصاحب التاريخ الأبعد أولى وإن ادعيا الشراء من واحد وأقاما البينة على التاريخين فالأول أولى
cards.en: A kharij is someone not holding the thing. If two such people prove ownership with dates, the earlier date wins. If two people prove they bought from the same seller, with dates, the earlier buyer wins. (If they bought from two different sellers, they are equal. And a holder whose ownership is dated earlier beats an outsider.)

cards.ask: Nasir and Kamal both prove they bought the same field from Rafiq. Nasir's proof says 2010, Kamal's says 2015. Who gets it?
cards.source: وإن ادعيا الشراء من واحد وأقاما البينة على التاريخين فالأول أولى
cards.why: Two buyers from one seller: the earlier one wins.

cards.title: Born in his care
cards.ar: وإن أقام الخارج وصاحب اليد كل واحد منهما بينة بالنتاج فصاحب اليد أولى
cards.en: Nitaj means an animal being born to someone's own animal, in his care. If the holder and an outsider both prove this, the holder wins. The same goes for cloth that can only be woven once, and anything that cannot happen twice. If the outsider proves ownership and the holder proves he bought it from him, the holder wins. If each proves he bought it from the other, with no dates, both proofs fall.

cards.ask: Yahya holds a foal. Idris says the foal was born to his mare at his farm and brings proof. Yahya brings proof that it was born at his own farm. Who gets it?
cards.source: بينة بالنتاج فصاحب اليد أولى
cards.why: When both prove birth in their care, the holder wins.

cards.title: More witnesses
cards.ar: وإن أقام أحد المدعيين شاهدين والآخر أربعة فهما سواء
cards.en: If one claimant brings two witnesses and the other brings four, they are equal. More witnesses do not make a proof stronger.

cards.ask: Rafi brings two witnesses for his claim and Hasan brings four for his. What does al-Quduri say?
options: Rafi wins because he came first
cards.source: وإن أقام أحد المدعيين شاهدين والآخر أربعة فهما سواء
cards.why: The number of witnesses beyond what is needed does not count. Their proofs are equal.

cards.ask: Does one side win, or are they equal?
items: Purchase against gift, both taken, no dates
Holder against outsider, both proving birth in their care
Purchase against a woman's claim it was her mahr
Two buyers from two different sellers, both dated
source: فالشراء أولى
فالرهن أولى
فصاحب اليد أولى
وادعت امرأة أنه تزوجها عليه فهما سواء
والآخر أربعة فهما سواء
وإن أقام كل واحد منهما بينة على الشراء من آخر وذكرا تاريخا فهما سواء
cards.why: Purchase beats gift, pledge beats gift, and the holder wins on birth. Purchase and mahr, two and four witnesses, and buyers from different sellers are equal.

lessons.title: Retaliation claims and who must answer

cards.title: Refusing to swear in qisas
cards.ar: ومن ادعى قصاصا على غيره فجحد استحلف فإن نكل عن اليمين فيما دون النفس لزمه القصاص وإن نكل في النفس حبس حتى يقر أو يحلف
cards.en: Qisas is equal retaliation for a deliberate injury. If someone claims qisas and the other denies it, he is made to swear. If he refuses for an injury less than a life, he owes the qisas. If he refuses in a claim about a life, he is held in prison until he admits or swears. Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say he owes compensation money in both.

cards.ask: Hamid claims Rafi broke his tooth on purpose and asks for qisas. Rafi denies it and refuses to swear. What is the ruling?
options: Rafi is imprisoned until he admits or swears
cards.source: فإن نكل عن اليمين فيما دون النفس لزمه القصاص
cards.why: For injuries less than a life, refusing to swear makes him owe the qisas.

cards.ask: A claim of killing is brought against Sa'id. He denies it and refuses to swear. What happens?
options: He is held until he admits or swears
cards.source: وإن نكل في النفس حبس حتى يقر أو يحلف
cards.why: For a life, refusal does not bring qisas; he is held until he admits or swears.

cards.title: Waiting for witnesses
cards.ar: وإذا قال المدعي: لي بينة حاضرة قيل لخصمه: أعطه كفيلا بنفسك ثلاثة أيام فإن فعل وإلا أمر بملازمته إلا أن يكون غريبا على الطريق فيلازمه مقدار مجلس القاضي
cards.en: If the claimant says "My witnesses are in town", the defendant is told to give a kafil (a guarantor who will bring him back) for three days. If he won't, the claimant may stay with him. But if he is a traveller passing through, the claimant stays with him only for the length of the judge's sitting.

cards.ask: Ahmad tells the judge, "My witnesses are in town." For how long must Bilal give a guarantor?
cards.source: أعطه كفيلا بنفسك ثلاثة أيام
cards.why: Al-Quduri says three days.

cards.title: "Someone left it with me"
cards.ar: وإن قال المدعى عليه: هذا الشيء أودعنيه فلان الغائب أو رهنه عندي أو غصبته منه وأقام بينة على ذلك فلا خصومة بينه وبين المدعي
cards.en: If the defendant says "An absent person left this with me", or "pledged it to me", or "I took it from him by force", and proves it, there is no case between him and the claimant. He is only holding it for someone else.

cards.title: "I bought it from him"
cards.ar: وإن قال: ابتعته من الغائب فهو خصم
cards.en: But if he says "I bought it from the absent person", he is the opponent and must answer the claim.

cards.ask: Zayd claims a bicycle held by Umar. Umar proves that Khalid, who is away, left it with him for safekeeping. What happens?
options: Umar must still answer the claim
Umar must hand it to Zayd
cards.source: فلا خصومة بينه وبين المدعي
cards.why: Umar is only keeping it for someone else, so there is no case between him and Zayd.

cards.ask: Does the case against the holder go on?
items: Holder says "I bought it from the absent man"
Claimant proves it was stolen from him; holder proves someone left it with him
Holder proves an absent man pledged it to him
Claimant says "I bought it from Fulan"; holder says "Fulan left it with me"
source: وإن قال: ابتعته من الغائب فهو خصم
وإن قال المدعي: سرق مني وأقام البينة وقال صاحب اليد:
فلان وأقام البينة لم تندفع الخصومة
أو رهنه عندي
وإن قال المدعي: ابتعته من فلان وقال صاحب اليد: أودعنيه فلان ذلك سقطت الخصومة بغير بينة
cards.why: A buyer must answer, and a claim of theft is not pushed away by a deposit. A proven pledge ends it, and if both name the same Fulan, the case drops even without proof.

cards.title: By Allah only
cards.ar: واليمين بالله تعالى دون غيره ويؤكد بذكر أوصافه ولا يستحلف بالطلاق ولا بالعتاق
cards.en: The oath in court is by Allah alone. It can be made stronger by naming His qualities. No one is made to swear by divorce or by freeing a slave.

cards.ask: The claimant asks the judge: "Make him swear that his wife is divorced if he is lying." May the judge do this?
options: No: the oath is by Allah, not by divorce
cards.source: ولا يستحلف بالطلاق ولا بالعتاق
cards.why: Al-Quduri says no one is made to swear by divorce.

cards.title: Other faiths
cards.ar: بالله الذي أنزل التوراة على موسى
cards.en: A Jew swears "By Allah who sent down the Torah to Musa". A Christian swears "By Allah who sent down the Injil to 'Isa". A Majusi (fire-worshipper) swears "By Allah who created fire".

cards.ask: How does a Jewish man swear in court? Complete it.
cards.ar: بالله الذي أنزل ____ على موسى
cards.source: بالله الذي أنزل التوراة على موسى
cards.why: التوراة: the Torah was sent down to Musa.

cards.title: No special place or time
cards.ar: ولا يحلفون في بيوت عباداتهم ولا يجب تغليظ اليمين على المسلم بزمان ولا بمكان
cards.en: They are not made to swear in their houses of worship. And a Muslim's oath does not have to be made heavier by a special time or place.

cards.ask: Which are true about the court oath?

options.text: It is by Allah alone
It can be made stronger by naming Allah's qualities
A Christian swears by Allah who sent the Injil to 'Isa
A Muslim must swear in the mosque
A Jew must swear inside a synagogue

source: واليمين بالله تعالى دون غيره ويؤكد بذكر أوصافه
بالله الذي أنزل
على عيسى
ولا يحلفون في بيوت عباداتهم
بزمان ولا بمكان
cards.why: The oath is by Allah, may name His qualities, and names the Injil for a Christian. No place, mosque or synagogue, is required.

cards.title: Wording for a sale
cards.ar: ومن ادعى أنه ابتاع من هذا عبده بألف فجحد يستحلف بالله ما بينكما بيع قائم فيه ولا يستحلف بالله ما بعت
cards.en: The oath is about the situation now. If someone claims he bought a thing for 1,000 and the other denies it, the denier swears "By Allah, there is no standing sale between you", not "By Allah, I did not sell".

cards.ask: Ahmad claims he bought Malik's horse for 1,000. Malik denies it. What does Malik swear?
options: By Allah, there is no standing sale between us
By Allah, I did not sell
By Allah, I never saw Ahmad
cards.source: يستحلف بالله ما بينكما بيع قائم فيه
cards.why: He swears about the present: no sale stands between them now.

cards.title: Wording for taking by force
cards.ar: بالله ما يستحق عليك رده ولا يحلف بالله ما غصبت
cards.en: In a claim of ghasb (taking something by force), he swears "By Allah, you do not owe its return", not "By Allah, I did not take it".

cards.title: Wording for marriage and divorce
cards.ar: وفي النكاح بالله ما بينكما نكاح قائم في الحال وفي دعوى الطلاق بالله ما هي بائن منك الساعة بما ذكرت ولا يستحلف بالله ما طلقتها
cards.en: For marriage: "By Allah, there is no standing marriage between you now." For a claim of divorce: "By Allah, she is not separated from you at this moment by what she said", not "By Allah, I did not divorce her".

cards.ask: A woman claims her husband divorced her. He denies it. How does he swear?
options: By Allah, she is not separated from me now
By Allah, I did not divorce her
By my wife's divorce, I did not
source: بالله ما هي بائن منك الساعة بما ذكرت
ولا يستحلف بالله ما طلقتها
cards.why: He swears about the present state, not "I did not divorce her".

cards.ask: In a claim of taking by force, what is the oath? Complete it.
cards.ar: بالله ما يستحق عليك ____
cards.source: بالله ما يستحق عليك رده
cards.why: رده: he swears that he does not owe its return.

cards.title: All and half
cards.ar: وإذا كانت دار في يد رجل ادعاها أحدهما جميعها والآخر نصفها وأقاما البينة فللصاحب الجميع ثلاثة أرباعها ولصاحب النصف ربعها عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: If a third man holds a house, one person claims all of it and another claims half, and both prove it, Abu Hanifa gives three quarters to the one claiming all and a quarter to the one claiming half. Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say it is split in thirds.

cards.title: When they both hold it
cards.ar: ولو كانت في أيديهما سلمت لصاحب الجميع: نصفها على وجه القضاء ونصفها لا على وجه القضاء
cards.en: If the two of them hold the house together, it all goes to the one claiming all of it: half by ruling, and half because no one else claims it.

cards.ask: Ali and Hasan live together in a house. Ali claims all of it and Hasan claims half, and both prove it. Who gets it?
options: All of it goes to Ali
Three quarters to Ali, a quarter to Hasan
cards.source: ولو كانت في أيديهما سلمت لصاحب الجميع
cards.why: When it is in both their hands, it all goes to the one claiming all of it.

cards.title: The animal's age
cards.ar: وإذا تنازعا في دابة وأقام كل واحد منهما بينة أنها نتجت عنده وذكرا تاريخا وسن الدابة يوافق أحد التاريخين فهو أولى وإن أشكل ذلك كانت بينهما
cards.en: If two people dispute an animal, each proving it was born with him and giving a date, the one whose date fits the animal's age wins. If it is unclear, it is shared between them.

cards.ask: Two men claim a camel. One says it was born with him four years ago, the other says ten years ago. The camel is clearly about four. Who gets it?
options: The one who said four years
The one who said ten years
cards.source: وسن الدابة يوافق أحد التاريخين فهو أولى
cards.why: The date that fits the camel's age wins.

cards.title: Riding, carrying, wearing
cards.ar: وإذا تنازعا دابة أحدهما راكبها والآخر متعلق بلجامها فالراكب أولى
cards.en: If two people dispute an animal, one riding it and the other holding its reins, the rider has the better claim. The same goes for a camel carrying one person's load, and a shirt that one person is wearing while the other holds its sleeve.

cards.ask: Majid is riding a mule; Sami is holding its bridle. Both say it is theirs, and neither has proof. Who has the better claim?
cards.source: فالراكب أولى
cards.why: Riding shows more control than holding the reins, so the rider comes first.

cards.ask: Who has the better claim?
items: The one wearing the shirt (other holds the sleeve)
The owner of the load on the camel
The one whose date matches the animal's age
Both prove birth, and the animal's age is unclear
source: فاللابس أولى
وعليه حمل لأحدهما الحمل أولى
يوافق أحد التاريخين فهو أولى
وإن أشكل ذلك كانت بينهما
cards.why: Wearing, carrying the load and the matching date each win. If the age is unclear, it is shared.

cards.title: Whoever proves it
cards.ar: وإذا اختلف المتبايعان في البيع فادعى أحدهما ثمنا وادعى البائع أكثر منه أو اعترف البائع بقدر من المبيع وادعى المشتري أكثر منه وأقام أحدهما البينة قضي له بها
cards.en: If buyer and seller disagree, the buyer naming a price and the seller a higher one, or the seller admitting an amount of goods and the buyer claiming more, whoever brings proof is ruled for.

cards.title: Both have proof
cards.ar: وإن أقام كل واحد منهما البينة كانت البينة المثبتة للزيادة أولى
cards.en: If both bring proof, the proof that shows the larger amount wins.

cards.ask: A seller proves the price was 1,200; the buyer proves it was 1,000. Which wins?
options: The seller's 1,200: it shows the larger amount
cards.source: كانت البينة المثبتة للزيادة أولى
cards.why: The proof for the larger amount comes first.

cards.title: No proof
cards.ar: وإن لم تكن لكل واحد بينة قيل للمشتري: إما أن ترضى بالثمن الذي ادعاه البائع وإلا فسخنا البيع
cards.en: If neither has proof, the buyer is told: "Accept the seller's price, or we cancel the sale." The seller is told: "Hand over the goods the buyer claims, or we cancel the sale."

cards.title: Both swear
cards.ar: فإن لم يتراضيا استحلف الحاكم كل واحد منهما على دعوى الآخر يبتدئ بيمين المشتري فإذا حلفا فسخ القاضي البيع بينهما وإن نكل أحدهما عن اليمين لزمه دعوى الآخر
cards.en: If they still don't agree, the judge makes each swear against the other's claim (this is tahaluf), starting with the buyer. If both swear, the judge cancels the sale. If one refuses, he is bound by the other's claim.

cards.ask: With no proof on either side, put the steps in order.
steps: Each is asked to accept the other's claim, or the sale is cancelled
source: قيل للمشتري:
فإن لم يتراضيا استحلف الحاكم كل واحد منهما على دعوى الآخر يبتدئ بيمين المشتري فإذا حلفا فسخ القاضي البيع بينهما
cards.why: First the offer to accept, then the oaths starting with the buyer, and when both have sworn the sale is cancelled.

cards.ask: With no proof, the buyer swears, but the seller refuses to swear. What happens?
options: The seller is bound by the buyer's claim
cards.source: وإن نكل أحدهما عن اليمين لزمه دعوى الآخر
cards.why: Whoever refuses the oath is bound by the other's claim.

cards.title: Disagreeing on terms
cards.ar: وإن اختلفا في الأجل أو في شرط الخيار أو في استيفاء بعض الثمن فلا تحالف بينهما والقول قول من ينكر الخيار والأجل مع يمينه
cards.en: If they disagree about an ajal (a later date for paying), a khiyar (an option to cancel), or whether part of the price was paid, they do not both swear. The word of the one who denies the option or the later date is taken, with his oath.

cards.ask: The buyer says "We agreed I pay in a month." The seller says "No, payment was due now." Neither has proof. Whose word is taken?
options: The seller's, with his oath: he denies the later date
Both swear and the sale is cancelled
cards.source: والقول قول من ينكر الخيار والأجل مع يمينه
cards.why: There is no tahaluf over a deadline. The one denying it is believed with his oath.

cards.title: When the goods are gone
cards.ar: وإن هلك المبيع ثم اختلفا لم يتحالفا عند أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف وجعل القول قول المشتري
cards.en: If the goods are destroyed and then they disagree, Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf say they do not both swear; the buyer's word is taken. Muhammad says they both swear and the sale is cancelled on the value of what was destroyed.

cards.title: One of two items gone
cards.ar: وإن هلك أحد العبدين ثم اختلفا في الثمن لم يتحالفا عند أبي حنيفة إلا أن يرضى البائع أن يترك حصة الهالك وقال أبو يوسف: يتحالفان ويفسخ العقد في الحي
cards.en: If one of two items sold together (al-Quduri's example is two slaves, in his time) is lost and they then disagree on the price, Abu Hanifa says they do not both swear, unless the seller agrees to drop the lost one's share. Note: Abu Yusuf says they both swear and the sale is cancelled for the one remaining; Muhammad says it is cancelled for both, with the value of the lost one returned.

cards.ask: Which word completes it?
cards.ar: كانت البينة المثبتة ____ أولى
cards.source: كانت البينة المثبتة للزيادة أولى
cards.why: للزيادة: when both prove, the proof showing the larger amount wins.

lessons.title: Disputes over mahr, rent and kitaba

cards.title: Proof of the mahr
cards.ar: وإذا اختلف الزوجان في المهر فادعى الزوج أنه تزوجها بألف وقالت: تزوجتني بألفين فأيهما أقام البينة قبلت بينة
cards.en: If husband and wife disagree on the mahr, he saying 1,000 and she 2,000, whichever brings proof is accepted.

cards.ask: Both the husband (1,000) and the wife (2,000) bring proof. Whose is accepted?
cards.source: وإن أقاما البينة فالبينة بينة المرأة
cards.why: When both prove, the woman's proof is taken.

cards.title: No proof: the usual mahr
cards.ar: وإن لم تكن لهما بينة تحالفا عند أبي حنيفة ولم يفسخ النكاح ولكن يحكم مهر المثل
cards.en: With no proof, Abu Hanifa says they both swear, but the marriage is not cancelled. Instead the mahr al-mithl decides it: the usual mahr for women like her.

cards.title: How mahr al-mithl decides
cards.ar: فإن كان مثل ما اعترف به الزوج أو أقل قضي بما قال الزوج وإن كان مثل ما ادعته المرأة أو أكثر قضي بما ادعته المرأة وإن كان مهر المثل أكثر مما اعترف به الزوج وأقل مما ادعته المرأة قضي لها بمهر المثل
cards.en: If the usual mahr is the husband's figure or less, his figure is given. If it is the wife's figure or more, hers is given. If it is in between, she gets the usual mahr.

cards.ask: Husband says 1,000, wife says 2,000, no proof. What is she given?
source: فإن كان مثل ما اعترف به الزوج أو أقل قضي بما قال الزوج
وإن كان مثل ما ادعته المرأة أو أكثر قضي بما ادعته المرأة
قضي لها بمهر المثل
cards.why: At or below his figure, his figure; at or above hers, hers; in between, the usual mahr.

cards.title: Disputes over rent
cards.ar: تحالفا وترادا وإن اختلفا بعد الاستيفاء لم يتحالفا وكان القول قول المستأجر
cards.en: Ijara is hiring or renting. If renter and owner disagree before the renter has used what he hired, both swear and the deal is undone. If they disagree after he has used it, they do not both swear, and the word of the musta'jir (the renter) is taken. If part has been used, they swear and the deal is cancelled for the rest, and the renter's word is taken for the past.

cards.ask: Wahid rented a shop for a year. After the year, the owner says the rent was 600; Wahid says 500. No proof. Whose word is taken?
options: Both swear and the deal is undone
cards.source: وإن اختلفا بعد الاستيفاء لم يتحالفا وكان القول قول المستأجر
cards.why: The year has been used, so they do not both swear, and the renter's word is taken.

cards.title: The kitaba
cards.ar: وإذا اختلف المولى والمكاتب في مال الكتابة لم يتحالفا عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, a mukatab was a slave buying his freedom from his master by payments (kitaba). If they disagree on the amount, Abu Hanifa says they do not both swear. Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say they both swear and the kitaba is cancelled.

cards.ask: Sara rented a house for 12 months. After 6 months, she and the owner disagree on the rent, with no proof. What happens?
options: They both swear; the rest is cancelled; her word is taken for the 6 months
Her word is taken for the whole year
cards.source: عليه تحالفا وفسخ العقد فيما بقي وكان القول في الماضي قول المستأجر
cards.why: Part is used: both swear, the rest of the deal is cancelled, and the renter's word stands for the past months.

lessons.title: Household goods and a child's lineage
lessons.arabic: وإذا اختلف الزوجان في متاع البيت

cards.title: Household goods
cards.ar: وإذا اختلف الزوجان في متاع البيت فما يصلح للرجال فهو للرجل وما يصلح للنساء فهو للمرأة وما يصلح لهما فهو للرجل
cards.en: If husband and wife disagree over the things in the home, what suits men is the man's, what suits women is the woman's, and what suits both is the man's.

cards.ask: A married couple dispute the household goods. Whose is it?
source: فما يصلح للرجال فهو للرجل وما يصلح للنساء فهو للمرأة وما يصلح لهما فهو للرجل
cards.why: Men's things go to him, women's to her, and things for both go to the man while both are alive.

cards.title: When one has died
cards.ar: وإذا مات أحدهما واختلف ورثته مع الآخر فما يصلح للرجال والنساء فهو للباقي منهما
cards.en: If one of them has died and the heirs disagree with the one still living, what suits both men and women goes to the living spouse. Abu Yusuf says the woman is given what a woman like her brings as her household goods, and the rest is the husband's.

cards.ask: Khalid has died. His heirs and his widow Maryam disagree over a carpet that suits both. Who gets it?
cards.source: فما يصلح للرجال والنساء فهو للباقي منهما
cards.why: After a death, what suits both goes to the one still living.

cards.title: A child born after a sale
cards.ar: فادعاه البائع فإن جاءت به لأقل من ستة أشهر من يوم البيع فهو ابن البائع
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, a master might sell a slave woman who then gives birth. If the seller claims the child and it is born less than six months after the sale, it is the seller's son. The mother becomes his umm walad (a slave mother of her master's child, freed at his death), the sale is cancelled and the price returned. The seller's claim comes before the buyer's.

cards.ask: In al-Quduri's time: a woman was sold, and gave birth four months later. The seller says the child is his. What is the ruling?
options: The child is the seller's son, and the sale is cancelled
The seller's claim is not accepted
The child belongs to the buyer
cards.source: فإن جاءت به لأقل من ستة أشهر من يوم البيع فهو ابن البائع
cards.why: Under six months from the sale, the child is the seller's.

cards.title: After six months
cards.ar: وإن جاءت به لأكثر من ستة أشهر لم تقبل دعوى البائع فيه إلا أن يصدقه المشتري
cards.en: If the child is born more than six months after the sale, the seller's claim is not accepted unless the buyer agrees.

cards.title: If the child or mother dies
cards.ar: وإن مات الولد فادعاه البائع وقد جاءت به لأقل من ستة أشهر لم يثبت الاستيلاد في الأم
cards.en: If the child has died and the seller then claims it, the mother does not become his umm walad. If the mother has died, the child's lineage from the seller is proven and he takes the child. Abu Hanifa says he returns the whole price; Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say only the child's share.

cards.title: Twins
cards.ar: ومن ادعى نسب أحد التوأمين ثبت نسبهما منه
cards.en: Whoever claims one of twins as his child is proven to be the father of both.

cards.ask: A man claims one of two twin boys as his son. What is the ruling?
options: Both twins are proven to be his
cards.source: ومن ادعى نسب أحد التوأمين ثبت نسبهما منه
cards.why: Twins come from the same pregnancy, so claiming one proves both.

cards.ask: Complete the time limit.
cards.ar: فإن جاءت به لأقل من ____ أشهر من يوم البيع فهو ابن البائع
cards.source: فإن جاءت به لأقل من ستة أشهر من يوم البيع فهو ابن البائع
cards.why: ستة: under six months from the sale, the child is the seller's.

lessons.title: A duty, and how many witnesses

cards.title: Testimony is a duty
cards.ar: الشهادة: فرض يلزم الشهود اداؤها ولا يسعهم كتمانها إذا طالبهم المدعي
cards.en: Shahada (testimony) means telling the judge what you saw or heard. It is a duty (fard). When the mudda'i (the person making a claim in court) asks the witnesses to speak, they must give their testimony and may not hide it.

cards.ask: Khalid saw Umar borrow 500 dirhams from Salim. Umar now denies the loan, and Salim asks Khalid to testify. What must Khalid do?
options: He must testify: he may not hide it
He may stay silent if he likes
He testifies only if Salim pays him
cards.source: يلزم الشهود اداؤها ولا يسعهم كتمانها إذا طالبهم المدعي
cards.why: Testimony is a duty: when the claimant asks, the witness must give it and may not hide it.

cards.title: Hadd cases: covering is better
cards.ar: والشهادة في الحدود يخير فيها الشاهد بين الستر والإظهار والستر أفضل
cards.en: Hudud (singular hadd) are the fixed punishments set by Allah, such as for theft. In a hadd case the witness may choose between covering up the sin (satr) and making it known. Covering it is better.

cards.title: Theft: say "he took"
cards.ar: إلا أنه يجب أن يشهد بالمال في السرقة فيقول: أخذ ولا يقول: سرق
cards.en: But in a theft the owner's money is at stake, so the witness must testify about the money. He says "He took it", not "He stole it". That way the owner gets his property back, while the sin itself stays covered.

cards.ask: What does the witness say in a theft case? Complete it.
cards.ar: فيقول: ____ ولا يقول: سرق
cards.source: فيقول: أخذ ولا يقول: سرق
cards.why: أخذ (he took): he testifies to the money but does not say "he stole".

cards.title: Zina, other hudud, and qisas
cards.ar: والشهادة على مراتب: منها الشهادة في الزنا يعتبر فيها أربعة من الرجال ولا تقبل فيها شهادة النساء ومنها الشهادة ببقية الحدود والقصاص تقبل فيها شهادة رجلين ولا تقبل فيها شهادة النساء
cards.en: Testimony has levels. For zina (unlawful relations) four men are needed, and women's testimony is not accepted. For the other hudud and for qisas (equal punishment for an injury or killing), two men are accepted, and women's testimony is not.

cards.title: Every other right
cards.ar: وما سوى ذلك من الحقوق تقبل فيها شهادة رجلين
cards.en: For every other right, two men are accepted, or a man and two women. It makes no difference whether the right is money or not, such as nikah (marriage), talaq (divorce), wakala (appointing an agent) and a will.

cards.ask: How many witnesses are needed?
into: Two men, or a man and two women
items: Two men, or a man and two women
Two men, or a man and two women
Two men, or a man and two women
source: منها الشهادة في الزنا يعتبر فيها أربعة من الرجال
ومنها الشهادة ببقية الحدود والقصاص تقبل فيها شهادة رجلين ولا تقبل فيها شهادة النساء
سواء كان الحق مالا أو غير مال مثل النكاح مثل النكاح والطلاق والوكالة والوصية
cards.why: Zina needs four men. Other hudud and qisas need two men. Every other right, money or not, takes two men or a man and two women.

cards.title: One woman alone
cards.ar: وتقبل في الولادة والبكارة والعيوب بالنساء في موضع لا يطلع عليه الرجال شهادة امرأة واحدة
cards.en: For things that men do not see, such as a birth, whether a woman is a virgin, and hidden defects of women, the testimony of one woman is accepted.

cards.title: Uprightness and the word "I testify"
cards.ar: ولا بد في ذلك كله من العدالة ولفظ الشهادة فإن لم يذكر الشاهد لفظ الشهادة وقال: أعلم أو أتيقن لم تقبل شهادته
cards.en: In all of these, the witness must have 'adala (be upright and trustworthy) and must use the word of testimony: "I testify" (ashhadu). If he says "I know" or "I am certain" instead, his testimony is not accepted.

cards.ask: In court Hamza says: "I am certain that Zayd owes Amr 100 dirhams." He never says "I testify". Is this accepted as testimony?
options: No: he did not use the word of testimony
Yes: being certain is even stronger
Yes, if a second witness agrees
cards.source: فإن لم يذكر الشاهد لفظ الشهادة وقال: أعلم أو أتيقن لم تقبل شهادته
cards.why: Without the word "I testify", saying "I know" or "I am certain" is not accepted.

cards.ask: Which of these can be proved by the testimony of one woman alone?
options: A birth that only women attended
source: وتقبل في الولادة والبكارة والعيوب بالنساء في موضع لا يطلع عليه الرجال شهادة امرأة واحدة
أو رجلين وامرأتين سواء كان الحق مالا أو غير مال
cards.why: One woman is accepted for a birth, where men do not see. A loan or a nikah needs two men or a man and two women, and a theft needs two men.

lessons.title: Checking witnesses, and what a witness may testify to

cards.title: Abu Hanifa: the outward uprightness
cards.ar: وقال أبو حنيفة: يقتصر الحاكم على ظاهر عدالة المسلم إلا في الحدود والقصاص فإنه يسأل عن الشهود وإن طعن الخصم فيهم سأل عنهم
cards.en: Abu Hanifa says the judge (hakim) may rely on a Muslim witness looking upright from the outside. But in hudud and qisas he asks about the witnesses, and if the other side attacks the witnesses, he asks about them too.

cards.title: Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad
cards.ar: وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: لا بد أن يسأل عنهم في السر والعلانية
cards.en: Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say the judge must always ask about the witnesses, both secretly and openly.

cards.ask: In a qisas case, two Muslim witnesses who look upright testify. What does the judge do about them?
options: He asks only if they are women
cards.source: إلا في الحدود والقصاص فإنه يسأل عن الشهود
cards.why: In hudud and qisas the judge asks about the witnesses before relying on them.

cards.ask: In a debt case, the man being sued says: "These witnesses are not honest people!" What does the judge do?
options: He ignores it, because it is not a hadd case
He throws out the whole claim
cards.source: وإن طعن الخصم فيهم سأل عنهم
cards.why: When the opponent attacks the witnesses, the judge asks about them.

cards.title: Things that stand by themselves
cards.ar: وما يتحمله الشاهد على ضربين: أحدهما: ما يثبت حكمه بنفسه مثل البيع والإقرار والغصب والقتل وحكم الحاكم فإذا سمع ذلك الشاهد أو رآه وسعه أن يشهد به وإن لم يشهد عليه
cards.en: What a witness takes on is of two kinds. The first stands by itself: a sale, an iqrar (admitting you owe something), ghasb (taking by force), a killing, a judge's ruling. If the witness heard or saw it, he may testify to it, even if nobody asked him to be a witness.

cards.title: "He sold", not "he made me witness"
cards.ar: ويقول: أشهد أنه باع ولا يقول: أشهدني
cards.en: Then he says "I testify that he sold". He does not say "he made me a witness", because no one did.

cards.ask: Bilal overheard Yusuf sell his camel to Idris. Nobody asked Bilal to be a witness. May he testify to the sale?
options: Yes: he heard it, and a sale stands by itself
No: he must be asked to witness first
cards.source: فإذا سمع ذلك الشاهد أو رآه وسعه أن يشهد به وإن لم يشهد عليه
cards.why: A sale stands by itself, so whoever heard or saw it may testify, even without being asked.

cards.title: Testimony on testimony needs permission
cards.ar: ومنه ما لا يثبت حكمه بنفسه مثل الشهادة على الشهادة فإن سمع شاهدا يشهد بشيء لم يجز أن يشهد على شهادته إلا أن يشهده وكذلك لو سمعه يشهد الشاهد على شهادته لم يسع السامع أن يشهد
cards.en: The second kind does not stand by itself, like testifying about someone else's testimony. If you hear a witness testify to something, you may not pass on his testimony unless he asks you to. Even if you hear him ask another person to carry his testimony, you, who only overheard, may not.

cards.ask: Sara heard Ahmad testify about a debt. Ahmad never asked her to carry his testimony. Later Ahmad is ill and cannot come to court. May Sara testify on his testimony?
options: No: he did not ask her to
cards.source: فإن سمع شاهدا يشهد بشيء لم يجز أن يشهد على شهادته إلا أن يشهده
cards.why: Testifying on someone's testimony needs that witness to ask you. Just hearing it is not enough.

cards.title: Your own handwriting
cards.ar: ولا يحل للشاهد إذا رأى خطه أن يشهد إلا أن يذكر الشهادة
cards.en: If a witness sees his own handwriting (for example on a paper he signed as a witness), he may not testify from it unless he actually remembers the event.

cards.ask: Umar finds a paper with his own handwriting saying he witnessed a sale, but he cannot remember the sale at all. May he testify?
options: No, not unless he remembers it
Yes: it is his own handwriting
Yes, if the paper is old
cards.source: ولا يحل للشاهد إذا رأى خطه أن يشهد إلا أن يذكر الشهادة
cards.why: Seeing his own handwriting is not enough. He may testify only if he remembers it.

cards.ask: May the witness testify?
items: He heard a man admit a debt
He saw a judge give a ruling
He overheard a witness testify, and was not asked to carry it
He sees his own handwriting but does not remember
source: مثل البيع والإقرار والغصب والقتل وحكم الحاكم فإذا سمع ذلك الشاهد أو رآه وسعه أن يشهد به
لم يجز أن يشهد على شهادته إلا أن يشهده
إلا أن يذكر الشهادة
cards.why: A killing, an admission and a ruling stand by themselves, so he may testify. Testimony on testimony needs permission, and handwriting alone is not enough.

cards.title: The blind, the slave, and the one punished for qadhf
cards.ar: ولا تقبل شهادة الأعمى ولا المملوك ولا المحدود في قذف وإن تاب
cards.en: The testimony of these is not accepted: a blind man, a slave (in al-Quduri's time), and one who was given the hadd for qadhf (falsely accusing someone of zina), even if he has repented.

cards.title: Close family and spouses
cards.ar: ولا شهادة الوالد لولده وولد ولده ولا شهادة الولد لأبويه وأجداده ولا تقبل شهادة أحد الزوجين للآخر
cards.en: A father may not testify for his child or grandchild, and a child may not testify for his parents or grandparents. A husband and wife may not testify for each other.

cards.ask: Hasan testifies that his grandson is owed 300 dirhams. Is his testimony accepted?
options: No: a grandfather cannot testify for his grandchild
Yes: only a father is blocked
cards.source: ولا شهادة الوالد لولده وولد ولده
cards.why: A father may not testify for his child or his child's child.

cards.title: Master, partner, brother and uncle
cards.ar: ولا شهادة المولى لعبده ولا لمكاتبه ولا شهادة الشريك لشريكه فيما هو من شركتهما وتقبل شهادة الرجل لأخيه وعمه
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time a master could not testify for his slave or his mukatab (a slave buying his freedom in instalments). A business partner may not testify for his partner about their shared business. But a man may testify for his brother and his uncle.

cards.ask: Yasir testifies that his brother Ammar lent 1,000 dirhams to a neighbour. Is it accepted?
options: Yes: a brother may testify for his brother
No: family may never testify for each other
Only if a woman testifies with him
cards.source: وتقبل شهادة الرجل لأخيه وعمه
cards.why: A man's testimony for his brother and uncle is accepted. Only parents, children and spouses are blocked.

cards.title: Shameful ways of living
cards.ar: ولا تقبل شهادة مخنث ولا نائحة ولا مغنية ولا مدمن الشرب على اللهو ولا من يلعب بالطيور ولا من يغني للناس
cards.en: Not accepted: a man who openly behaves in an indecent, effeminate way; a woman paid to wail at funerals; a singing woman; one who keeps drinking for fun; one who plays with birds (racing pigeons); and one who sings for people.

cards.title: Major sins and low behaviour
cards.ar: ولا من يأتي بابا من الكبائر التي يتعلق بها الحد ولا من يدخل الحمام بغير إزار أو يأكل الربا ولا المقامر بالنرد والشطرنج ولا من يفعل الأفعال المستخفة كالبول على الطريق والأكل على الطريق
cards.en: Also not accepted: one who commits a major sin that carries a hadd; one who enters the public bath without a waist-cloth; one who eats riba (interest on loans); one who gambles with backgammon or chess; and one who does shameless things, like urinating or eating in the street.

cards.ask: Whose testimony is NOT accepted?

options.text: A man who eats riba
A man who gambles at chess
A man who eats in the street
A man testifying for his uncle
A man born of zina

source: أو يأكل الربا ولا المقامر بالنرد والشطرنج
والأكل على الطريق
وتقبل شهادة الرجل لأخيه وعمه
والخصي وولد الزنا
cards.why: Eating riba, gambling and eating in the street block testimony. Testifying for an uncle is accepted, and so is a man born of zina.

cards.title: Beliefs, dhimmis and harbis
cards.ar: ولا تقبل شهادة من يظهر سب السلف وتقبل شهادة أهل الأهواء إلا الخطابية وتقبل شهادة أهل الذمة بعضهم على بعض وإن اختلفت مللهم ولا تقبل شهادة الحربي على الذمي
cards.en: Not accepted: one who openly insults the salaf (the early Muslims). People of mistaken beliefs (ahl al-ahwa) are accepted, except a group called al-Khattabiyya. Dhimmis (Jews and Christians living under Muslim rule) are accepted against each other, even of different religions. A harbi (from a land at war with Muslims) is not accepted against a dhimmi.

cards.ask: Faris avoids all major sins, and his good deeds are far more than his bad ones, but sometimes he slips into a small sin. Is his testimony accepted?
cards.source: وإن كانت الحسنات أغلب من السيئات والرجل ممن يجتنب الكبائر قبلت شهادته
cards.why: If his good deeds are more than his bad ones and he avoids major sins, his testimony is accepted even if he sometimes slips.

cards.title: These are accepted
cards.ar: وتقبل شهادة الأقلف والخصي وولد الزنا وشهادة الخنثى جائزة
cards.en: These are accepted: a man who is not circumcised, a eunuch, a person born of zina, and a khuntha (a person whose body is not clearly male or female).

cards.ask: Is the testimony accepted?
items: A Christian dhimmi against a Jewish dhimmi
A man punished for qadhf who has repented
A man who is not circumcised
source: وتقبل شهادة أهل الذمة بعضهم على بعض وإن اختلفت مللهم ولا تقبل شهادة الحربي على الذمي
ولا تقبل شهادة أحد الزوجين للآخر
وتقبل شهادة الرجل لأخيه
ولا المحدود في قذف وإن تاب
وتقبل شهادة الأقلف
cards.why: Dhimmis against each other, a brother and an uncircumcised man are accepted. A harbi against a dhimmi, a spouse, and one punished for qadhf are not.

cards.title: Testimony must match the claim
